![](https://images.theconversation.com/files/756687/original/file-20260828-60-yzv85q.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&rect=0%2C0%2C4590%2C3060&q=45&auto=format&w=1050&h=700&fit=crop)

[Arun Sankar/Getty Images](https://www.gettyimages.com.au/detail/news-photo/general-view-shows-houses-lying-deluged-in-sludge-after-news-photo/2291686791?adppopup=true)

At around 8:45am on August 26, Karbir Gaire, a customs and information officer at Nepal’s Rasuwa Customs Office, [suddenly felt](https://english.ratopati.com/story/76780/my-heart-aches-when-i-remember-how-i-managed-to-escape-in-those-10-seconds) what seemed like an earthquake. He went outside, looked towards China and saw a huge flood accompanied by dust. He shouted, “The flood is coming, run!”

Gaire and others immediately ran uphill. About 10 seconds later, the muddy water swept away the structures around him.

Gaire later told local media outlet Ratopati those 10 seconds were decisive: people who recognised the danger and ran towards higher ground survived. Others who delayed or ran elsewhere were swept away, or went missing.

His experience captures a potentially life-saving truth: a warning only saves lives if it produces immediate action.

For Australia’s Nepalese community, including me and my family, this disaster is deeply personal. Families and friends across Australia are waiting anxiously for news of loved ones.

But beyond the immediate devastation, the disaster raises an important question: could lives be saved if people were trained to act immediately when a flood warning arrives?

I believe the answer is yes.

## Disaster in Nepal

The devastating August 26 flood [originated in the high Himalayas](https://theconversation.com/nepals-flash-floods-show-the-devastating-power-of-cascading-hazards-290611) near the Nepal-China border and sent a massive surge of water through the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli-Narayani river systems.

Hundreds of people have died, and many remain [missing in Nepal and Tibet](https://www.theguardian.com/world/live/2026/aug/28/nepal-tibet-flash-floods-hundreds-dead-missing-day-three-live-updates). At least 39 Australians have been reported missing.

It is important not to portray this disaster simply as a failure of warning. Nepal has an established flood forecasting and early-warning system, including hydrological [monitoring and mobile phone alerts](https://alnap.org/help-library/resources/monitoring-rivers-for-flood-early-warning-nepals-ingenious-solutions/).

The preliminary technical report from Nepal’s Flood Forecasting Division, as reported by [the news media](https://english.onlinekhabar.com/technical-report-rasuwa-flood.html), provides an important timeline. Authorities received information at about 9am that a flood had entered the Bhote Koshi from the Tibetan side. Between 9:15 and 9:16, some 600,000 [early-warning SMS messages](https://globalnation.inquirer.net/336186/how-the-nepal-flood-unfolded-over-10-hours) were sent to vulnerable communities in Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading and Chitwan.

The division says the timely dissemination of the warning helped many people reach safety.

The lesson, therefore, is not that early warning is useless. Rather, early warning must be connected to early action. For example, people need to understand what “evacuate” means.

[![A man walking through thick mud, passed ruined houses.](https://images.theconversation.com/files/756688/original/file-20260828-50-cnprj4.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&q=45&auto=format&w=754&fit=clip)](https://images.theconversation.com/files/756688/original/file-20260828-50-cnprj4.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.1.1&q=45&auto=format&w=1000&fit=clip)

A resident walks along a street covered in mud following flash floods and a landslide disaster in Devighat, in Nepal’s Nuwakot district on August 26, 2026.
[Prakash Mathema/Getty Images](https://www.gettyimages.com.au/detail/news-photo/resident-walks-along-a-street-covered-in-mud-following-news-photo/2291598715?adppopup=true)

## How do people react in emergencies?

My research on emergency evacuation behaviour provides relevant insights. In [one study](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ssci.2016.07.017), we surveyed 1,134 train passengers in Melbourne about how they would respond during an emergency evacuation. We found passengers were more likely to be reactive than proactive. For example, they were more likely to wait for instructions from station staff than to immediately move towards an exit themselves. They were also likely to follow what other passengers were doing.

In a [second study](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0925753519321952), we surveyed 950 passengers, 500 at Melbourne Airport and 450 at Qingdao International Airport in China, about how they would behave during an emergency. Importantly, we found passengers’ perceptions of how they would cope were related to their perceived ability to evacuate safely. This suggests that knowing what to do – such as following evacuation procedures and leaving belongings behind – can influence how confident people feel.

Although we examined transport emergencies rather than floods, the lessons are relevant: people should not have to work out what to do for the first time when disaster is already unfolding.

They should already know when to leave, where to go and how to reach safety. This shows the public needs to be prepared *before* emergencies occur.

We need to prepare the public for floods with a simple, rehearsed response. When an extreme flood warning is issued, people in vulnerable areas should already know their local evacuation procedure. They should be familiar with how to leave the river area and move to higher ground. They should not wait to see the water, return for possessions or attempt to save a vehicle.

## Technology is necessary, but not enough

Nepal needs continued investment in flood and rainfall monitoring, mobile alerts and community warning systems.

But the physical monitoring infrastructure is vulnerable: four automatic hydrological monitoring stations were [reportedly swept away in Nepal](https://english.onlinekhabar.com/technical-report-rasuwa-flood.html). Warnings should still be possible through alternative sensors, satellites, cameras, sirens, radio, public-address systems and trained local networks.

Nepal already has experience with community-based flood early-warning systems that combine monitoring, [communication and community preparedness](https://alnap.org/help-library/resources/monitoring-rivers-for-flood-early-warning-nepals-ingenious-solutions). In these systems, rising floodwaters can be detected in near-real time and warning information is transmitted to trained local caretakers, who relay it to vulnerable downstream communities and relevant authorities through channels such as SMS, mobile phones and sirens.

Education determines whether the warning becomes action.

## Recovery will take years

The immediate priority remains rescuing those who can be found, locating the missing, treating the injured, and providing food and medical assistance.

But recovery will extend far beyond the immediate rescue operation.

Homes, roads, bridges, schools and livelihoods will need to be restored, while survivors may need long-term psychological and social support.

Reconstruction should therefore aim not simply to rebuild what was lost, but to build back safer, with stronger infrastructure, resilient communication networks, better evacuation routes and better-prepared communities.

The tragedy of Nepal’s floods reminds us we cannot prevent every extreme event but we can improve people’s chances of survival. An effective early-warning system is measured not only by how many warnings it sends but also by whether people understand them and act in time. As one survivor’s experience shows, sometimes just 10 seconds can mean the difference between life and death.

For those who lost their lives, and for the families still waiting for loved ones, my deepest thoughts and prayers are with you. The most meaningful tribute to those lost is to learn from this tragedy and build a safer, better-prepared future.

![The Conversation](https://counter.theconversation.com/content/290725/count.gif)

*Nirajan Shiwakoti receives funding from the Australian government and other research funding organisations for research on transport, mobility and emergency evacuation. He is of Nepali origin and has a personal connection to Nepal, where he has family and community ties. He has no financial or commercial interests in the technologies, organisations or infrastructure discussed in this article.*

entries.title: Silo showrunner Graham Yost breaks down episode 9s bombshell ending and surprise musical guest
entries.content:
![Jessica Henwick, Ashley Zukerman, and Reed Birney in ](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/06u72LTTXbII91yvGRoJ3Mv/hero-image.jpg)

[*Silo* Season 3, episode 9](https://mashable.com/entertainment/silo-season-3-episode-9-ending-explained) ended not with a bang, but with a nuclear blast that shook the show to its core.

In the episode's final sequence, congressman Daniel (Ashley Zukerman) and journalist Helen (Jessica Henwick), now expecting a child, visit the silos on their first day open to outside civilians. The event is ritzy as can be, complete with beautiful landscaping around the Silo entrances and a surprise Peter Gabriel concert. But something about it feels off. Why is shady operative Henry (Reed Birney) so intent on separating Daniel and Helen? Why won't Daniel's sister Charlotte (Jessica Brown Findlay) respond to Daniel's texts?

SEE ALSO:
['Silo' Season 3, episode 9's shocking ending, explained](https://mashable.com/entertainment/silo-season-3-episode-9-ending-explained)

The wrongness comes to a head as Daniel and Helen try to reunite with one another. Just as they catch sight of each other on the berms ringing their respective silos, a nuclear bomb explodes in the distance. As the blast races towards them, Daniel is dragged back to Silo 1, and Helen's fate is left unknown. (Given that her Pez dispenser winds up in Silo 18, I'm betting she made it back inside.)

It's a harrowing sequence that finally reveals the calamity that blighted the area around all the silos and sets the stage for a potentially game-changing finale. Mashable spoke with *Silo* showrunner Graham Yost about the show's latest explosive twist, as well as [AI](https://mashable.com/category/artificial-intelligence)'s role in writing the Pact, Peter Gabriel's surprise concert, and whether Jimmy (Steve Zahn) could be one of Gabriel's long-lost descendants.

**One detail of this episode that cracked me up but also gave me a bit of an existential crisis was the reveal that Anna (Morven Christie) and Victor (Matt Craven) "wrote" the Pact, which is such a foundational text for Silo residents, using AI. Tell me about including that detail, and how it speaks to the Founders' attitudes toward the Silo dwellers.**

**Graham Yost:** I'll say, I don't use AI. But whenever I use Google, I'm using AI now, because I can ask a very specific question like, "How old was FDR's Secretary of State in 1940?" and up it comes. I don't have to find out who he was and then look at his life and do the math. So we all use AI now to a degree. I don't use it that much. I don't have an AI persona in my life, but a lot of people do. We felt that that was a cool way to explain how something like the Pact could be written.

There was one version where there was a team of social scientists who were building this and writing this, and then I was like, "No, let's just say it's AI." It became a joke, which was fun, and the fact that Victor kind of laughed at it, almost like it's not that important. What's important is what happens in the bigger story and how it's acted upon in the people's lives.

SEE ALSO:
[What's new to streaming this week?](https://mashable.com/entertainment/new-to-streaming-august-28-2026)

**I think the last few minutes of episode 9 took years off my life, from the nuclear explosion to the lead up. For you, what do you think makes a truly great apocalypse scene, and how did you want to bring those qualities to life in *Silo*?**

We had to just kind of do our own thing and set it aside. *Fallout* starts with a nuclear explosion, and Walton Goggins is there witnessing it. I wrote a movie called *Broken Arrow* which had an underground nuclear explosion which, for visual effects back in 1996, was pretty awesome, [with] the ground rising up and then sinking down. It's not new.

The trick for us was Helen and Daniel. That's what makes it. It's these two people that we've grown to love, and they're torn apart by it, so that was the story for us.

**I'd love to hear more about building that dread around their separation, because as soon as he's being sent to Silo 1 and she's being sent to Silo 18, you know it's over.**

That's Amber Templemore, our director. There's some stuff where we are so in sync, and sometimes she'll do things, [and I'll worry] "maybe that's too much." Then I see it, and I go, "No, we're doing a television series. We're trying to be entertaining. We're trying to do this." We have to thread this needle between hiding the ball and giving a hint that the ball is going to come rolling down.

Then Atli Örvarsson, our composer, when Daniel is sitting over at Silo 1 and he's texting Charlotte, Atli does this faint "ding." It's just this little sound, it's just this little thing, and it's also Ash [Zukerman]'s performance. Now you start to realize, and it builds. There's Reed Birney [who plays Henry] saying, "Daniel, you have to come with me," and people telling Helen, "You can't go up on [the berm]." You just know something bad is going to happen, and guess what? Something bad happens! It's a build in the script, it's a build in the design, it's a build by Amber.

![Colin Hanks and Laura Innes in "Silo."](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/06u72LTTXbII91yvGRoJ3Mv/images-1.fill.size_2000x1125.v1787774930.jpg)

Colin Hanks and Laura Innes in "Silo."
Credit: Apple TV

**I do have to say, this attack is *very* suspiciously timed to the first day the silos are open to civilians.**

[*laughs*] What? That's weird.

***So* weird.**

I don't know. We didn't think about that!

**But it seems pretty obvious that something is going on. We see Per Stensen get a message as he leaves the stage. I'm curious, will we find out more about the actual events leading up to the bombing? Was it a part of his master plan?**

[*laughs*] You'll have to pay to find that out.

**I also loved the Peter Gabriel cameo. It feels like a full circle moment after using "Come Talk to Me" at the end of Season 3, episode 1. We learn that he and his family are living in Silo 17, so there's a chance Jimmy or the other kids are Peter Gabriel descendants. Can you canonically confirm or deny?**

I can canonically confirm. There's a non-zero chance. We did not actually walk that through. There are some family bloodlines that we have discussed.

But the Gabriel thing goes back to Season 2, when Solo/Jimmy is trying to lure Juliette (Rebecca Ferguson) back to the vault door because he wants to talk to her about something. He plays "Red Rain" by Peter Gabriel, so that music exists in Silo 17. That's why we knew he had to go into 17.

[Gabriel and I] got to know each other through the show. I'd approached him about something in Season 1, and it didn't work out. But we connected, and we'd been talking about other things. He ended up watching the show with his family, and they loved it. So I said, "Would you do this thing?" He said, "Yeah, I'm free. Can I bring my son, and can he can he bring his girlfriend?" I said, "Sure." So that's his son and his son's girlfriend at the side of the stage.

Will Smith, the showrunner on *Slow Horses*, he and I bonded over Peter Gabriel back in the early days of *Slow Horses*. So I told him, "Hey, you've got to come to set on this day." He'd been one other day because it's a fun set to visit, but this was outside. I didn't tell him [about Peter Gabriel]. We were walking from his car to set, and Peter's coming the other way to go to his trailer, and [Smith] says, "Is that him?" I said, "Yeah." He said, "Fuck me." So we got to hang out with Peter and his son and his son's girlfriend, just making a TV show. That was a fun day.

**That's delightful. There's nothing like a Peter Gabriel performance before the end of the world.**

And the song, "Here Comes the Flood." Reed Birney said to me on the day, "it's a little on the nose, isn't it?" I said, "Reed, we're doing a TV show. It is." Hopefully the audience doesn't realize when Peter's singing "say goodbye to flesh and blood" that in fact we're going to see a nuclear weapon go off later.

*The interview above was edited for length and clarity.*

[*Silo* Season 3 is now streaming on Apple TV. The finale premieres Sept. 4.](https://zdcs.link/Qp2BZg?pageview_type=RSS&template=article&module=content_body&element=offer&item=text-link&element_label=Silo%20Season%203%20is%20now%20streaming%20on%20Apple%20TV.%20The%20finale%20premieres%20Sept.%204.&object_type=article&object_uuid=06u72LTTXbII91yvGRoJ3Mv&short_url=Qp2BZg&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmashable.com%2Ffeeds%2Frss%2Fall "(opens in a new window)")

entries.title: Silo Season 3, episode 9s shocking ending, explained
entries.content:
![Jessica Henwick and Ashley Zukerman in ](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/07Is6B0oU8adiH4NZBRxlju/hero-image.jpg)

Well, that was unexpected.

Back in [*Silo*](https://mashable.com/article/silo-review-apple-tv) Season 3, episode 7, we were finally [shown the founders responsible for building the silos](https://mashable.com/entertainment/silo-season-3-episode-7-who-built-silos). In episode 8, we seemed to get a clue as to [how the world might end](https://mashable.com/entertainment/silo-season-3-episode-8-how-the-world-ends) — and now episode 9 has gone and turned the whole thing on its head.

So, what happens at the end of episode 9, and what does it all mean? Let's unpack it.

SEE ALSO:
['Silo' showrunner Graham Yost breaks down episode 9's bombshell ending and surprise musical guest](https://mashable.com/entertainment/silo-season-3-episode-9-graham-yost-interview)

## What happens at the end of *Silo* Season 3, episode 9?

A lot happens in episode 9, from Bernard (Tim Robbins) being sent out to die to Camille (Alexandria Riley) having her faith in [the mysterious algorithm](https://mashable.com/entertainment/silo-algorithm-human) shaken. The last half of the episode, though, is something else. We cut from chaos in the silo to our flashback storyline, only now we've jumped forward in time: Daniel (Ashley Zukerman) and Helen (Jessica Henwick) are expecting a baby, and they're visiting the now-complete silo system that Per Stensen (Colin Hanks) and Senator Thurman (Laura Innes) have been working on for the past three years.

In this future, the silos are already operational, and people have been living in them for the past year as part of the experiment. Daniel and Helen are there for a tour ahead of the grand unveiling. Only as they're shown around, it feels like there's a tension in the air — like the founders know more than they're letting on.

While Helen is led to Silo 18 (yep, that's *our* silo), Daniel is taken by Henry (Reed Birney) and Dr. Victor Crnkovich (Matt Craven) to Silo 1, where he meets with Senator Thurman and Per Stensen, who are busy practising their speeches.

Daniel's sister Charlotte (Jessica Brown Findlay), however, is nowhere to be found. And when Daniel texts her their family in-joke ("If mom and dad were alive right now..."), she sends the wrong response back.

Sensing something's off, Daniel gets Helen on the phone. She's walking up the ramp of Silo 18 to try and get a phone signal. Henry follows him, telling him he has to come back, but Daniel ignores him and climbs to the top of the silo's berm.

"I got a text from Charlotte, but I don't think she wrote it," he tells Helen through a crackling phone line. Finally, she reaches the top of Silo 18's berm, and they catch sight of each other in the distance. But midway through their exchange, everything suddenly turns white-red. There's a ringing sound. And once the light dims, we see the horrific sight of a mushroom cloud on the horizon. As Daniel struggles to reach Helen, he's wrestled back down towards Silo 1 by Henry and another guard, while a robotic voice tells them over and over again to seek shelter in the nearest silo.

At the end of the episode, it's unclear whether he, or Helen, have survived.

## Did we just witness the end of the world?

Yes, that much at least seems clear. The mushroom cloud on the horizon looked like a nuclear missile, presumably the event that triggers a global apocalypse and turns the planet into the wasteland Juliette (Rebecca Ferguson) and the others see outside in the present day.

What's interesting is the event isn't what we thought it was going to be: In episode 8, Per Stensen seems convinced that nanotechnology is the biggest threat to humanity — but it appears he was wrong after all.

## Who was responsible for the nuclear explosion?

This is the big question we still don't have the answer to. In episode 8, Stensen says Iran and the U.S. are at war with each other over Iran's development of nanoweapons, so instinctively you might suspect Iran is behind the explosion.

But if that's the case, why are so many of the founders — and those closest to them — acting as if they know something's about to happen? Charlotte's partner Anna (Morven Christie), who is also the daughter of Senator Thurman, looks distant throughout the episode, insisting they need to get to the silos early and looking awkward when Daniel suggests they do breakfast the following day. Per Stensen seems distracted. And Henry immediately tries to bring Daniel back to Silo 1 when he wanders away on the phone. What do they know that Daniel and Helen don't?

And if they do know about an impending nuclear attack, why has nobody informed U.S. intelligence agencies? Why are they just letting it happen?

SEE ALSO:
['Silo' Season 3, episode 8: We may finally know how the world ends](https://mashable.com/entertainment/silo-season-3-episode-8-how-the-world-ends)

One final thing worth pointing out is a throwaway line from Helen's Silo 18 tour guide, who cheerfully tells her about the silo's capabilities.

"This silo was built to withstand a 30-megaton nuclear explosion as close as two miles," he says. Given what happens a short time later, that seems awfully specific. The silo was built to withstand a nuclear explosion in very close proximity — which is *exactly* what ends up happening. Surely that's too much of a coincidence?

## Who wrote The Pact?

The ancient document known as The Pact is something akin to a bible for residents of the silo, and now we finally know who was behind it: Anna Thurman and psychologist Dr. Crnkovich, who apparently wrote it together as a kind of psychological survival manual.

"It's some crazy shit she and Dr. C wrote," Charles tells Helen the night before the silo visit. "It is a book of rules about how to live underground for 500 years without killing each other."

Dr. Crnkovich later tells Daniel that the silo project is largely about "managing mass trauma."

He does admit, though, that he and Anna didn't write the whole thing by themselves.

"To be honest, AI wrote it," he says. "We just did some editing."

## What will happen to Helen and Daniel?

Although we don't see either of them making it to safety, both Helen and Daniel are close to the entrances of Silo 18 and Silo 1, respectively, when the nuclear explosion hits. Given that they're both main characters, it seems unlikely that their journeys end here. So, what's next?

Well, the fact that Helen ends up in Silo 18 is surely no coincidence. Although the apocalypse takes place hundreds of years before the events we've witnessed in present-day Silo 18, the fact that Helen is pregnant could mean her descendants are still alive in the future. Could she and Daniel be related to one of the main characters in Juliette's Silo 18?

Daniel, meanwhile, is last seen being dragged towards Silo 1, the core silo that we now know acts as a kind of central hub for the whole silo system. Given the way Henry separates him and Helen at the start of the tour, it seems clear that Daniel has been marked out for Silo 1 intentionally, likely for his engineering brain.

If he survives, our guess is the founders will have had a specific use in mind for him.

[*Silo* Season 3 is streaming now on Apple TV, with new episodes dropping every Friday.](https://zdcs.link/kWx85?pageview_type=RSS&template=article&module=content_body&element=offer&item=text-link&element_label=Silo%20Season%203%20is%20streaming%20now%20on%20Apple%20TV%2C%20with%20new%20episodes%20dropping%20every%20Friday.&object_type=article&object_uuid=07Is6B0oU8adiH4NZBRxlju&short_url=kWx85&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmashable.com%2Ffeeds%2Frss%2Fall&session_uuid=74a76c63-7258-4780-bde2-f01e4ba6a8c6&view_instance_uuid=389d5d5b-c832-47e3-bb7d-db45bb83917a "(opens in a new window)")

entries.title: Canada Hires 48 Scholars Away From Top US Universities
entries.content:
Canada is recruiting 64 researchers to universities across the country (source paywalled; alternative source), including 48 from U.S. institutions such as Harvard, Yale, and MIT. The hires are backed by more than $364 million in government funding and are part of a broader effort to attract researchers in fields such as AI, climate science, and medicine. The New York Times reports: While scientists often shy away from political discourse, some are saying the Trump administration's assault on science is behind their departure. "I used to live in the country that I thought was the most enthusiastic about the prospects for science improving the human condition, of any country in the world," said Phillip Zamore, the chair of RNA Therapeutics Institute at the University of Massachusetts. "And I woke up one day and that wasn't true anymore." He has been recruited to McGill University in Montreal, which has also hired five other researchers, and will join the medical faculty. "If scientists don't stand up for truth, no one will," Dr. Zamore said.
The Canada-bound brain drain from U.S. institutions began last year as the Trump administration put forward policies that targeted foreign students, academic freedom and funding for equity-related programs. Kevin Hall, a nutrition scientist who left the U.S. National Institutes of Health last year, accusing federal officials of censoring his research on ultraprocessed foods, has been hired at the University of Ottawa. "While certain countries are cutting research and turning their back on academic freedom, we're doubling down on science," Melanie Joly, Canada's industry minister, told reporters at the announcement, in Vancouver, of the new university hiring. She billed it as the world's "largest talent attraction" project. The European Union has made a similar push. "Years from now, we will look back at today's announcement, and we will be able to seize the lasting impact of our choices," Ms. Joly said.
Unpredictable decisions about funding prompted Seth Guikema, a professor in civil and environmental engineering, who has specialized in natural hazards modeling at the University of Michigan, to look elsewhere. His work focuses on how climate hazards inequitably affect communities, and that work has become harder to fund, he said. "Every country sets its priorities in terms of what is going to get funded, and I think Canada has done a very good job of supporting research in areas that really matter to society," said Dr. Guikema, who will start at Western University in London, Ontario in January.

[![](https://a.fsdn.com/sd/twitter_icon_large.png)](http://twitter.com/home?status=Canada+Hires+48+Scholars+Away+From+Top+US+Universities%3A+https%3A%2F%2Fnews.slashdot.org%2Fstory%2F26%2F08%2F27%2F2350251%2F%3Futm_source%3Dtwitter%26utm_medium%3Dtwitter)

entries.title: Exec couldn’t identify a photocopier, which made for a fax-inating tech support call
entries.content: ON CALL By the end of the working week it can be tempting to phone it in, but The Register instead works to bring you extra amusement in the form of a new edition of On Call – the reader-contributed column that shares your tech support stories. This week, meet a reader we’ll Regomize as “Orson” who told us they very much enjoyed the recent On Call about the lawyer who didn’t understand italics. “It reminded me of an incident many years ago when I was a Facilities Manager for a major UK food company,” Orson told On Call. “I came in one morning and was summoned by the Company Secretary, who was clearly annoyed because the night before, she tried to send an extremely urgent fax and the fax machine did not work.” For those who don’t remember fax machines, or successfully tried to forget them, they packed a low-res scanner, a nasty printer, and a slow modem into a small appliance. The user interface included a numeric keypad used to enter the phone number of whichever remote fax machine you wanted to send a document to. Faxes were horrible, but faster than the postal service. Email killed faxes in the late 1990s (except in Japan) though manufacturers kept including fax functions in multifunction printers (MFPs) for years. But we digress: Orson decided the way to solve this problem was to start with the wetware. “I asked her to show me what she had done and watched as she placed the document on the in-tray, used the keypad to dial the number, and then hit Enter,” he told On Call. Having gone through those steps, the Company Secretary stared at Orson, her pose clearly communicating a desire for him to swiftly explain why technology had let her down – and why the facilities team had left the fax machine in such a state. “I told her she was trying to use the photocopier,” Orson told On Call. To be fair, the presence of MFPs in many workplaces meant that wasn’t a completely horrible mistake. But as an example of a rather silly tech support moment, it makes for a fine On Call! Does a similar tale lurk in your memory? If so, click here to send your story to On Call. We’d offer to let you fax it in, but The Register doesn’t have a fax machine anymore. ®

entries.title: Print management outfit PaperCut is under 0-day attack, and it’s drawing customers’ blood
entries.content: Nothing smarts like a paper cut, but being attacked after leaving an application’s web interface exposed to the internet might be just as painful. Such attacks are the risk to which users of PaperCut print management software find themselves exposed today, after the company revealed a university’s security teams alerted it to an attack. The company analyzed info provided by the university and found a vulnerability in its PaperCut NG and PaperCut MF products, which manage access to printers, track use, and enable printing from myriad client devices. “We are aware of confirmed customer incidents and are treating this matter with the highest priority,” states an urgent security advisory issued on Thursday. Unusually, the advisory is silent on the nature of the flaw and the risk it poses. It looks like the web interface to the company’s products enables access deeper into a user’s networks, because among the indicators of compromise are altered log files, plus alerts from intrusion detection software, endpoint security tools, and network monitoring packages. The company has cooked up an emergency patch but warns it is not an official release. “We have not gone through our usual release process,” states an FAQ. “This is an emergency patch for customers with public-facing PaperCut servers who are unable to take other mitigating action.” Thankfully, those other actions aren’t hard to take: users need to get their PaperCut servers’ web interfaces off the public internet, by allowing access only from trusted internal IP addresses. Fashioning a potent and rapid response to a zero-day attack is never easy. Communicating the nature of the problem can be even harder, as discussing the nature of a flaw invites more attackers to take a shot at a stricken product. PaperCut says it’s working on a better fix and will advise users once it lands. For now, the company is asking customers to apply its wonky patch or take their servers offline ASAP. The Register fancies most users will go for the latter fix, as aside from the issue of finding a change window in which to apply a patch, running unvalidated emergency software is not an appetizing approach. ®

entries.title: Australian cops cuff alleged TeamPCP masterminds
entries.content: The Australian city of Perth is by some measures the world’s most isolated major metropolis, but is still sufficiently connected to US law enforcement authorities that the FBI was able to help Australia’s Federal Police (AFP) to find two men they believe were the masterminds of TeamPCP, a cybercrime crew that conducted prominent supply chain attacks. According to the AFP, two men aged 21 and 23 arrested on Wednesday “were principal participants in the activities of the cybercrime syndicate and received payments in cryptocurrency for their roles in the illegal activity.” An FBI Facebook post names one of the arrested men as Ruben Thomson and describes him as “the alleged leader of the cybercriminal group TeamPCP.” Australian media named the second man as 23-year-old Louis Michael Gaebler. Investigations into the pair started in April 2026, after Australian authorities and the FBI “received information from multiple cyber threat assessment companies regarding a syndicate that allegedly inserted malicious code into software available on an open-source repository, which was then unwittingly used by other developers.” Researchers detected some of those activities before April: In March, we reported that researchers spotted a supply chain attack on the open source scanner Trivy. Another of TeamPCP’s attacks was the Shai-Hulud worm, which attacks npm packages, tries to infect them and goes looking for credentials to major public clouds or services like GitHub. If the worm burrowed into its targets, it would either try to replicate to continue its attacks, or wipe the environment out of spite. The AFP’s “We cuffed ‘em!” announcement estimates that TeamPCP’s supply chain attacks “potentially compromised more than 1000 organisations globally, enabling the theft of more than 500,000 credentials, and the exfiltration of at least 300 gigabytes of data.” Australia’s Feds estimate “the financial impact includes global remediation costs estimated to be hundreds of millions of dollars.” As is often the case in such matters, the arrested men were found with electronic devices and other items which authorities seized. “A large volume of data seized is being forensically examined and the investigation remains ongoing,” the AFP wrote, adding “Further arrests and charges have not been ruled out.” Indeed, the Feds note that they arrested the two at different locations in the suburbs of Perth and searched a third property nearby. ® Bootnote: Perth is considered the site of the original “Black Swan” event, as swans there – and across much of Australia – are black. Early European explorers who explored Australia's west coast were astounded when they saw the black birds, as the “fact” that all swans are white was at the time a metaphor for the existence of absolute truths.

entries.content:

A recent discovery revealed that AliExpress employs silent audio streams for device fingerprinting, leveraging the Web Audio API. This technique involves analyzing hardware-specific audio processing to distinguish user devices. Privacy-focused browsers have developed countermeasures, highlighting a security gap in current web standards regarding audio context initialization and user privacy.

*By Olimpiu Pop*

entries.title: BOFH: Schrödinger's petty cash puts us in a very awkward superposition
entries.content: EPISODE 16: "So it looks like we have ourselves a Schrödinger's cash situation," I say. "We have a what now?" asks the very junior beancounter - the sort that will be first up against the wall when the AI revolution comes (in a couple of weeks). "A Schrödinger's cash situation. You have a petty cashbox with a variable amount of money in it, which depletes at an unknown rate. Depletion being what it is, at some point the cashbox will have no cash in it. If I ask you to open your cashbox - and pay out my expenses - I can guarantee that you'll say the cashbox is empty." "It is empty," he replies. "Only it's NOT empty," the PFY says, "because we can see the petty cash spreadsheet reflected off the glass of the picture on the wall behind you." "You couldn't read that. It'd be back to front." "Back to front like 8753?" I ask. "Sorry?" "8753 - the reverse of the PIN number you used to unlock your computer just now," I say. "How did..." "Or 'now here they're," the PFY adds, "the reverse of the quick email you sent when we came in." "I.." "Let's just say that we have a particular set of skills, skills acquired over very long careers..." I say. "Reading reflected letters, upside down words, etc. Anyway, we'd really appreciate it if you'd reimburse us now." ... No one likes petty cash. Beancounters hate it because they have to handle actual cash, and everyone else hates it because the petty cash reimbursement process is subject to a level of scrutiny that His Majesty's Customs and Revenue can only aspire to. "Your receipts don't outline what they were used for," the junior beancounter states. "Yes, they do, I wrote the detail on the back." "Yes, but that's just a cash register receipt. It could be from anywhere. You need a proper receipt." "The Petty Cash Policy states that we only need a detailed receipt for anything over five pounds, and you'll note that these receipts are for a maximum of..." "Four Pounds 99," he nods. "Yes, I noticed. But there's no detail on the receipts about where they were from. You could have been buying pints, one at a time." "Know many pubs with an actual cash register, do you?" I ask. "It doesn't matter. You say you were buying thumb drives. But there's no proof, and the combined value is over 5 pounds." "If you look at the register timestamps, you'll see that they were all bought at different ti…" "Yes, but you shouldn't buy them with your own money anyway. You should have been using the purchasing system to order a batch of thumb drives." "Well, if we're talking about what people should be doing, then perhaps your Boss shouldn't have been letting his kids trash his laptop, so that he needed a new laptop, AND THEN insisting on the bitlocker key for his new machine be saved to a USB stick, ASAP." "I don't know anything about that. Anyway, you need to get these receipts signed off by someone with financial authority in your department." "Ah, so we move into Heisenberg's uncertainty principle of Boss movements," the PFY notes. "The what?" "Heisenberg's uncertainty principle of Boss movements." "Is this some quantum thing?" "At the microscopic, everything is a quantum thing. But no, the problem with the Boss is you might know where he is, but you never know where he's going. If you know where he's going, you can never actually be sure where he is. Because he gets sidetracked. So, if you want him to sign off small expenses you have to create a situation that brings him to his office." "So... you call him?" "Calling him will only tell you where he is, but (crucially) not where he's going." "So you ask him where he's going?" "No, because of the sidetrack thing. You need to creat an event where you know he will definitely go to his office." "An event like what." "A serious complaint usually works," the PFY suggests. ... "YOU PUSHED HIS LAPTOP OFF THE TABLE!" the Boss snaps angrily. "It fell off the table," I explain, turning to the PFY. "Didn't it?" "It did. We both saw it," the PFY agrees. "So anyway, while you're here, could we get your John Hancock on these expenses forms?" ... "And here we are, with our expenses forms all signed," I say happily. Our junior Beancounter scrutinizes each receipt carefully, ensuring that it concurs with the amounts detailed in the form. One by one, he enters them into his mildly dented laptop, verifies the totals on his spreadsheet match those on the signed forms in front of him. "So, rounded to the nearest coin we have... That's... 38 pounds, 40p for you and 29 pounds, 35p for you." "Sounds right to me," I say. "And me," the PFY says. "OK, so I'll just get one of my colleagues to count out the actual cash and..." >jingle< >creak< >slam< "Okay, where's the Petty Cash tin gone?" he snaps. "That sounds like another of those quantum things," I say. "Schrödinger's cashbox. In theory, we all believed the cashbox existed - right up until you opened the drawer." "Really?" the PFY says. "I thought it was the same old Heisenberg's uncertainty of payment principle. Every time we come here to get reimbursed, we're never really sure what hoops we'll have to jump through to get paid." "So you stole the Petty cash tin?" "What? In a locked drawer that only you and your colleague have access to? A drawer that you've not strayed away from all morning?" "So you stole it last night?" "How could we? In fact, I'm fairly sure that the book on the shelf over there - with the suspicious looking round hole in its spine - will agree with our version of events. Maybe you didn't check the drawer properly. >creak< >slam< ... "You didn't happen to see a cat in there did you?" the PFY asks. entries.title: #691.Jen Abel：拿下 10 万美元企业大单的完整路径，别让 AI 热潮掩盖了销售基本功
entries.content:
📝 本期播客简介

本期我们克隆了：Lenny's Podcast: Product | Career | Growth How to close $100K+ enterprise deals, step by step | Jen Abel

原内容更新时间：Sun, 23 Aug 2026

本期节目由 Lenny Rachitsky 主持，邀请企业级销售专家 Jen Abel，完整拆解一笔 10 万至 100 万美元企业级交易从第一次触达、初次沟通、产品演示、试用期，到采购、合同审查和最终签字的全过程。Jen 曾三次做客 Lenny's Podcast：第一次讨论创始人主导销售，第二次讨论 100 万至 1000 万美元的企业级销售打法，而这一次，她把企业销售从大家熟悉的“五步漏斗”还原成接近 15 个真实步骤。

节目以向 SpaceX 法务部门销售 AI 法律科技为案例，讲清楚如何同时触达高管与 N-1 级别联系人，如何用“钳形模式”建立组织内部的推动力，如何在第一次电话中克制住演示冲动，先获取情报、识别真正的改变需求，再围绕客户语境设计演示和试用。Jen 反复强调，企业级销售不是把客户塞进自己的销售流程，而是帮助客户完成他们自己的采购流程。

这期内容尤其适合创始人、产品经理、企业级销售、客户成功负责人，以及正在从 SMB 转向大客户市场的创业团队。你会听到大量可直接执行的细节：为什么演示前要再打一通准备电话，为什么试用期最好严格控制在两三天，什么时候应该收取试用费用，为什么健康的企业销售赢单率只有约 25% 至 35%，以及如何避免采购、法务和内部意见分歧让交易失去势头。

👨‍⚕️ 本期嘉宾

Jen Abel，JJellyfish 联合创始人，同时担任 State Affairs 企业级销售总经理。她长期专注于早期创业公司的创始人主导销售、企业级客户拓展和高客单价交易，尤其擅长把看似依赖个人天赋的销售经验，拆解成可以理解、练习和复盘的具体步骤。

Jen 的独特之处在于，她并不把销售简化成一套固定话术或 CRM 阶段，而是同时强调流程、项目管理、信息优势和人与人之间的判断力。她认为，最优秀的销售往往不是接受过最多标准化培训的人，而是最会倾听、挖掘信息、理解组织目标，并能让客户对未来产生兴奋感的人。这也是她第三次做客 Lenny's Podcast，依然能提供大量一手经验的原因。

⏱️ 时间戳

开场：企业级销售为何不是五步漏斗

01:45 Jen Abel 登场：这次要完整走过企业级销售周期

03:26 15 步销售打法的目标：把秘密全部讲清楚

06:20 SpaceX 法务部门案例：从 10 万美元交易开始

07:35 10 万美元与 100 万美元交易，本质上是同一套流程

第一步：找到对的人，并用 Alpha 触达

09:27 第一步：如何约到第一次企业级销售会议

10:28 企业高管真正关心的是“超额收益”

11:49 钳形模式：同时触达高管与 N-1

15:19 用工具寻找关键联系人，但必须靠人工判断核对

第二步：初次沟通电话，先获取情报

18:51 初次沟通是所有电话里最重要的一通

19:53 非正式开场：让对方先说

21:36 不要急着把对话引向产品

23:10 为什么初次沟通千万不要录音

第三至六步：从跟进、准备到精准演示

30:11 初次沟通后的跟进：不要直接跳到 Demo

31:46 演示前的准备电话：和内部推动者一起设计故事线

35:12 最危险的 Demo：没有准备就向一群人展示产品

41:39 只展示 20% 最有价值的功能

试用期：用两三天验证价值并掌控节奏

49:31 确定试用期的推进流程

50:45 两种试用期：轻量验证与深度集成

53:24 和客户共同定义成功标准

54:49 在试用前倒推签约时间线与内部参与者

企业销售的真实漏斗与赢单率

1:03:39 CRM 的五个阶段不是实际销售流程

1:05:14 90% 的人误把 CRM 流水线当成销售打法

1:08:39 健康的企业级销售赢单率约为 25% 至 35%

1:10:58 从合格线索到 Demo，通常会流失一半

采购、合同与最终签字

1:05:37 第十步：试用期后的复盘与真实反馈

1:12:22 第十一步：合同准备与采购时间线

1:15:28 合同审查：把来回邮件变成实时会议

1:17:57 最后一步：确认签字人并完成签署

成交之后：扩张、拒绝与销售的长期价值

1:18:57 签单之后如何思考增购与扩张

1:19:12 企业级销售真正的核心是第二年的扩容

1:20:15 买家如何尽早、清楚地说“不”

1:22:37 销售和产品管理：本质上都是理解人和解决问题

🌟 精彩内容

💡 企业级销售不是五步，而是接近 15 步

Jen 认为，CRM 里的“介绍、演示、方案、合同、赢单”只是用于预测和加权的分类，并不代表客户真实经历的销售步骤。每一个 CRM 阶段背后，往往还需要数次关键沟通、内部协调和决策推动。把五步漏斗误认为真实流程，是企业销售团队最常见的认知错误之一。

“多数人以为销售流程就五步，而我们现在已经讲到第 10 步了，这都还没讲完。”

💡 高管买的不是问题解决，而是不对称的优势

向企业高管触达时，单纯说“我们能帮你解决某个问题”远远不够。高管需要看到的是，引入这套方案后，自己能为组织释放什么新的价值：更多影响力、更大预算、更高效率，或一种能向 CEO、COO 和董事会证明的实质性改变。

“最重要的是超额收益。”

💡 钳形模式：高管和 N-1 必须同时推进

Jen 建议创始人直接触达最高层决策者，同时让 AE 或企业销售负责人联系高管下面一层、最接近执行的人。两条线同时推进，既能获得高管级价值判断，又能拿到一线执行信息，避免销售故事在组织内部层层转述后失真。

“它其实就叫钳形模式，也就是从最顶层切入，找到那一层底线，然后在两者之间推进。”

💡 初次沟通的任务不是展示产品，而是让客户多说

第一通电话决定了客户是否会放下防备，也决定了销售能获得多少真实信息。不要急着打开 PPT、做 Demo 或追问标准化的 BANT 问题，而应该让对方先讲自己的目标、规划、组织变化与成熟度，再根据这些信息组织后续叙事。

“这是所有电话里最重要的一通。”

💡 不要照搬销售话术，真正的优势来自信息差

标准化话术会让销售变得同质化，预算、决策权、需求和时间点应该作为销售脑中的判断框架，而不是机械地逐项询问。谁能比竞争对手多理解客户的潜台词、内部关系和优先级，谁就能把 Demo、试用和商业方案做得更像是为客户量身打造。

“让自己沦为同质化最快的方式，就是套用一些销售话术。”

💡 两三天的试用，往往比两周的试用更有效

轻量试用的目标不是让客户自由探索产品，而是挑选三到四名真正的重度用户，为每个人设定清晰任务、提供上手培训，并与客户共同定义成功标准。把试用严格限制在 48 到 72 小时，既能更快验证价值，也能避免销售周期被无止境拉长。

“改成 48 到 72 小时，就能把你的销售周期缩短两周。”

💡 演示不是产品巡回展示，而是一次精准的叙事与项目管理

企业客户并不需要看到产品的全部功能。销售应该在前期沟通中找出最重要的 20% 价值，再围绕这部分内容组织 Demo，让客户产生“这就是为我们做的”感觉。展示过多无关功能，反而会让客户开始怀疑自己为什么要为一堆用不到的东西付费。

“企业级销售就是极其紧凑的项目管理，极其紧凑的叙事和框架，并且牢牢掌控这个框架。”

💡 健康的赢单率不是越高越好

合格商机从 Demo 到最终签约会持续流失，健康的企业级销售赢单率通常在 25% 至 35% 左右。如果赢单率异常高，可能意味着定价过低，或者团队没有充分筛掉尚未成熟、并不真正需要产品的客户。与其盲目追求更高赢单率，不如保持价格、做好资格审查，并为未来重新进入市场的客户留下空间。

“如果你的赢单率比这还高，说明你定得太便宜了。”

🌐 播客信息补充

本播客采用原有人声声线进行播客音频制作，也可能会有一些地方听起来怪怪的

entries.title: Scientists tested 212 plant-based meat alternatives. Every one contained fungal toxins
entries.content: Every one of 212 plant-based meat alternatives and drinks tested in the UK contained at least one naturally occurring fungal toxin, though concentrations remained below recommended EU guideline levels. Researchers say the bigger question is whether regularly eating large amounts of these foods could lead to potentially concerning cumulative exposure over time.

entries.title: Scientists tracked 4,500 animals and found a surprising human effect
entries.content: Scientists tracking thousands of animals found that our physical presence can reshape where wildlife moves and lives, sometimes as strongly as roads, cities, and other human development. Because different species reacted in very different ways, conservation efforts may need to become much more targeted.
entries.summary: 一项追踪4500只动物的研究显示，人类物理活动显著改变野生动物迁徙轨迹。

Sleep trackers — wearable devices that monitor all your vitals — provide detailed summaries of your sleep cycle so you know how many hours of REM, deep, and light sleep you're getting. Most [fitness trackers](https://mashable.com/roundup/best-fitness-trackers-1) come equipped with sleep tracking these days, but choosing the best from that bunch is not as straightforward. These days, sleep trackers come in all shapes and sizes, and fortunately, our experts here at Mashable have tested them all.

So if the magnesium supplements and pillow sprays in your [sleepmaxxing](https://mashable.com/article/sleepmaxxing-sleep-trend-tiktok) routine aren't working, here are the best sleep trackers of 2026.

entries.title: Cyberattack on UK Airport Operator MAG Exposes Data of 8.7 Million Customers Across Three Airports
entries.content:
## A cyberattack on Manchester Airports Group exposed data of 8.7 million customers across Manchester, Stansted, and East Midlands airports.

Manchester Airports Group disclosed that an unauthorised third party accessed customer data belonging to approximately 8.7 million people across three of England’s busiest airports: Manchester, London Stansted, and East Midlands.

*“Manchester, London Stansted and East Midlands airports have been hit by a cyber-attack in which hackers accessed the data of about 8.7 million customers.” reads the report published by The Guardian.*

*“The incident involved data related to “car park, lounge and fast-track bookings and in-airport wifi sign-ups”, and the hackers obtained email addresses, phone numbers, vehicle registration numbers and postcodes, said Manchester Airports Group (MAG), which operates the three hubs.”*

MAG says it learned about the incident on Tuesday, August 25, after attackers breached the system over the weekend.

The affected data included car park bookings, lounge and fast-track security reservations, and airport Wi-Fi sign-ups. Attackers accessed email addresses, phone numbers, vehicle registration numbers, and postcodes. The system did not store bank or payment details. According to MAG, most of the 8.7 million affected customers only lost their email addresses, while the impact varies depending on which services they used.

The attack did not disrupt airport operations or flights. As a precaution, MAG temporarily suspended its Manage My Booking service, but all existing reservations remain valid. Customers who need to change a booking within the next 72 hours can use a dedicated phone line.

*“We would urge you to be particularly cautious of unexpected emails, calls or text messages claiming to be from us. We will never contact you unexpectedly to ask for payment or banking information. We apologise for any inconvenience or concern this may cause.” reads the email sent by Stansted to affected customers.*

That warning is relevant because the combination of an email address, a phone number, and the knowledge that someone recently made a parking or lounge booking gives a convincing starting point for a targeted phishing message. Attackers don’t need payment data if they can impersonate the airport convincingly enough to obtain it themselves.

The timing adds pressure. The attack landed during the peak summer travel season, with millions of families flying back into the UK before the school year begins. The three airports combined handled around 54 million passengers last year, and MAG recently reported a record 66 million passengers across its network. The scale of the data exposure reflects the sheer volume of ancillary services these airports sell, and how much personal data those services routinely collect.

The wifi registration system is the detail worth noting: signing into airport wifi typically requires a name, email, and phone number at minimum, and that information now belongs to whoever executed this breach.

MAG says it quickly contained the incident, brought in external cybersecurity experts and notified the relevant authorities. No group has claimed responsibility, and investigators have not publicly linked the attack to any specific actor.

The incident adds to a growing list of cyberattacks against UK infrastructure. Earlier in August, Iran-linked hackers took a British power plant offline for four days, marking the first confirmed case of Iranian actors shutting down a UK generator. Last year, attacks disrupted production at Jaguar Land Rover and targeted Marks & Spencer, Harrods and the Co-op. Heathrow also faced flight delays and cancellations after attackers disrupted check-in and boarding systems used by several European airports.

MAG’s breach adds further pressure on UK infrastructure operators to strengthen their cyber defenses.

[**Pierluigi Paganini**](http://www.linkedin.com/pub/pierluigi-paganini/b/742/559)

![Windows 11 一口气更新21项新增功能，但一定先别着急更新 5](https://static3cdn.appinn.com/images/2026/08/Copy-of-appinn-homework-2026-08-28T151145.147-1.jpg "Windows 11 一口气更新21项新增功能，但一定先别着急更新 5")

## KB5120998 更新了什么？

注意这个版本是可选更新，所以你可以选择不更新，但会错过21项新功能。

但是，一旦更新，你可能会遇到几个莫名其妙的 bug…

![Windows 11 一口气更新21项新增功能，但一定先别着急更新 6](https://static3cdn.appinn.com/images/2026/08/CleanShot-2026-08-28-at-14.17.17@2x.avif "Windows 11 一口气更新21项新增功能，但一定先别着急更新 6")

在更新日志中，本次更新涉及方方面面，青小蛙就捡「新增」来说：

### 任务栏

* **新增！**任务栏终于可以显示在屏幕底部、顶部、左侧或右侧。
* **新增！**更小的任务栏选项
* **新增！**任务栏设置页面中的“**任务栏行为**”部分现在默认展开，以便于查找。

入口：**“设置”>“个性化”>“任务栏”>“任务栏行为”>“任务栏位置”** / **“****任务栏行为**”

### 开始菜单

* **新增！**可自定义选择小号或大号“开始”菜单
* **新增！** “开始”菜单和设置页面（**设置 > 个性化 > 开始**）中的“推荐”部分已更名为“最近”。
* **新增！**在开始屏幕上隐藏姓名和个人资料图片
* **新增！** “开始”菜单设置页面新增了分区级切换功能，可独立显示或隐藏“已固定”、“推荐”和“全部”等内容。

入口：**“设置”>“个性化”>“开始”**

### Windows 搜索

* **全新！**搜索主页已简化，减少了视觉混乱
* **新增！**搜索功能可以更好地显示搜索结果的来源——应用、设置、文件、网页结果或应用商店建议
* **新增！**允许选择是否将网络和 Microsoft Store 建议与本地搜索结果一起显示
* **新增！** Windows 现在会自动为常用文件夹建立索引

入口：**“设置”>“隐私和安全”>“搜索”**

### 文件资源管理器

* **新增！**启动文件资源管理器主页的速度更快、响应更灵敏。
* **新增！**首页的“推荐”部分现在支持触摸滚动，让您更容易浏览轮播图中的文件。

### 总体设计

* **全新！**新的更新进度指示器，在启动、登录、重启、关机和更新安装过程中提供更加一致和现代化的体验。

---

后面的功能，对普通用户关系不大。

### Windows 共享

* **新增！**为工作或学校帐户登录的用户新增了直接从共享窗口发现并安装相关应用的功能。

### 管理员保护

* **新增！** 管理员保护旨在保护管理员的自由浮动管理员权限。它允许用户使用即时权限执行管理任务。管理员保护不属于正式的安全边界；它通过引入配置文件分离来加强对权限提升攻击的防御。

### 微软商店

* **新增！**此更新为需要提升权限的打包 WinUI 3 应用提供应用内购买支持，帮助开发者通过微软的集成商务平台提供购买选项。

### Windows Autopilot 设备准备

* **新增！** Windows Autopilot 设备准备的设备关联功能现已正式发布。此功能可帮助组织在注册前识别受信任的设备，从而实现针对特定设备的策略、企业设备的自动注册，以及在开箱即用体验 (OOBE) 期间进行其他设置自定义。

### 微软执行容器

* **新增！**本次更新引入了 Microsoft 执行容器 (MXC) 的进程隔离功能，它为编码代理和模型生成代码等响应式工作负载提供了一个快速、轻量级的边界。

### 代理过程

* **新增！**本次更新引入了代理进程标记的预览平台支持。已授权组件可以将不透明的代理标识符分配给进程令牌。Windows 会保护此标记并自动将其传递给子进程。

### 密码学

* **新增！**后量子密码算法 ML-KEM 现在除了之前添加的混合组之外，还可以作为独立的 TLS 密钥交换算法使用。

## 遇到了什么问题？

虽然这个版本带来了不少新功能，其中自定义任务栏位置、缩小任务栏、在Windows 搜索中关闭网页搜索和微软商店搜索这几个功能还是非常实用的。

不过已经有不少用户反馈遇到了问题，其中包括：

1. **鼠标指针样式失效**
   * 自定义鼠标指针被重置。
   * 指针可能变成默认的白色、大尺寸样式。
   * 修改指针颜色、大小后可能无法正常生效。
   * 部分用户卸载 KB5120998 后恢复正常。
   * 这是目前反馈最集中、可信度最高的问题。
2. **桌面壁纸变成黑色**
   * 原来的桌面背景消失，变成纯黑背景。
   * 有些用户重新设置壁纸即可恢复。
   * 也有用户报告注销或重启后再次变黑。
   * 已有多个用户反馈，但并非普遍发生。
3. **个性化设置可能出现异常**
   * 从现有反馈看，问题主要集中在桌面个性化相关功能，包括鼠标指针、主题/背景。
   * 目前还无法确定具体触发条件，可能与自定义主题、指针、DPI/显示缩放等配置有关。
4. **DISM 可能出现 0x800f0915**
   * 有相关反馈，但这个错误在 KB5120998 之前已经存在。
   * **目前不能认定是 KB5120998 导致的**

但是，并没有**大规模的蓝屏、无法启动、文件丢失等严重问题**。

所以，更新了，又可能没更新。

entries.title: Article: Post-Quantum Cryptography in Spring Boot: Four Patterns You Can Ship This Sprint
entries.content:
![](https://res.infoq.com/articles/pqc-in-spring-boot/en/headerimage/pqc-in-spring-boot-header-1787646727709.jpg)

There are four patterns that bring PQC into a Spring Boot fleet: encrypting payloads between services, locking down database fields, signing documents that need to hold up for decades, and moving service tokens off RS256. Along the way, we discuss why Harvest Now, Decrypt Later is already happening, and why none of this is production-safe until KMS or Vault is in place.

*By Pankaj Sharma*

18金16银12铜，一共46枚奖牌。

首次出征，就在金牌榜和奖牌榜双榜登顶。可以说，智元这次是名副其实的冠军。

在16个国家、666支队伍、2056台机器人同台竞技的赛场上，智元机器人靠着全方位、无死角的实力，横扫全场。

更惊人的是，这些在赛场上大杀四方的机器人（远征A3、精灵G2、灵犀X2），和在龙旗工厂里打工的机器人，竟然完全是同一批。

用智元自己的话说，这是真正的「戴得了工牌，赢得了金牌」。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=cde3dfd8&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fsz_mmbiz_jpg%2FRvq8Ow69CYUYUDfHmUXTAuH8agtgPILWzLGjQsEYELY2E9631ibicy7CdMmgiayonibYrp1z2SXfgJdpyxicfLa6pXiariapH6JRibuELzAAA6Hw5ico%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Djpeg%26from%3Dappmsg)

**一只灵巧手，直接包揽7金！**

仔细看，它拿了第一的这些项目，简直堪称是地狱级难度。

面对极轻的粉末，OmniHand能够像经验丰富的老师傅一样，精准控制倾倒的角度和力度，稳稳拿捏住毫厘之差。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=34dc2a04&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fmmbiz_png%2FRvq8Ow69CYWzLX6HsZPV9RhPqVlnJJsIPIEF8KibWD3FSdicMz4bt7IG5C9BicXLvNVoJklAwhYqNc7qIr9zOYoojYxY1CFQtaQ0k8SS0n06HU%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dpng%26from%3Dappmsg)

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=1d2927a7&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fmmbiz_jpg%2FRvq8Ow69CYVr8ttFABNaqA3FxO41gks9kvsoyr56vVaSyibNfsNeWoYBBMVwDwABlB32HWWFJfwVx3yhXzGNloibVpBvYpibibRObicd73yLRREk%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Djpeg%26from%3Dappmsg)

过去，传统的机械手完全依赖提前写好的代码。但OmniHand，靠的是一颗聪明的「大脑」。

智元临界点为其量身自研了「DUET双层具身接触智能架构」。

它就像是人类的小脑和指尖神经的结合体。外层负责「位姿控制」，让手知道该怎么伸过去、角度怎么调整；内层则负责「触觉控制」，让机械手拥有人类皮肤般的「触觉感知」。

智元机器人和刘雨昕现场热舞

乒乓球赛场上，它还和奥运冠军丁宁打得有来有回。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=f92bc87b&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fmmbiz_jpg%2FRvq8Ow69CYUNoAsvBKlP3wugzTzxjTjvFwXAuuB76V0u0OXtQQhYIWx21Bq29qhIHLjv9fwjrvB7ahp8NylMbh5j15GaDBoRAM0EPYDXa8c%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Djpeg%26from%3Dappmsg)

即便是「双机」对战，接球动作依然是行云流水。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=a370afbc&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fmmbiz_gif%2FRvq8Ow69CYXl2buNQpxWK9pPrk4I4cEam57DNnhglSudgYWYNXP5ymia48ibhmgRWtlPibgn84wemIudxVv1PErd7icJft6JDnU64SpG0a0RhUA%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dgif%26from%3Dappmsg)

可以说，它不仅仅是在「动」，而是在挑战人形机器人的物理极限：腾空跳跃、大角度转体、单腿长时间支撑、甚至极其考验核心力量的低重心姿态无缝切换！

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=722712c6&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fmmbiz_gif%2FRvq8Ow69CYXxj1ia3F3Dq1VKib8ribMS7DZqKrICLGAVkibicKDvOicC6KdSX1FZggiaUM7Wc5McXQqAgGEjQLkPoAo9m5o1QodQwibZckj22t5eJqI%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dgif%26from%3Dappmsg)

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=7d4dc6e1&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fsz_mmbiz_gif%2FRvq8Ow69CYWHY3Jk4icDwbnYoFyDqAibzoicTibFKMobRqdE38MUY6TjElIjKozziavhOYU15syXJ5JZ4XcqRXfzFPSyULp1Ox6ibG7cfogD47sw0%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dgif%26from%3Dappmsg)

要完成这些动作，需要有毫秒级的全身姿态实时调控能力。

这一切，都依托于智元自研的运动预训练模型和全身协同控制算法。

通过「灵创平台」海量运动数据的投喂，它掌握了通用运动先验知识，并通过强大的Sim2Real能力，将仿真训练迁移到机器人。

而在田径赛场上，智元灵犀X2更是贡献出精彩表演。

在田径100米障碍赛和400米障碍赛中，灵犀X2在无任何本体改装的情况下，硬是斩获1金、1银、1铜。

面对赛道上的不规则障碍物，大多数参赛机器人还停留在仅依赖「关节本体感知」的阶段，但智元灵犀X2，却早早装上了「眼睛」。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=fa89eecb&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fmmbiz_gif%2FRvq8Ow69CYVgA3HSibjShodOmMz65PUqPrQUibTZtSDYlnPxOJpRqpe1vqZKyl2poFTl7WwIT6UicSgwhfmuibXgIRWk5mkZEwe5tJ30hwZ7hT0%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dgif%26from%3Dappmsg)

之前的机器人运动会，很多都在这一关折戟了，灵犀X2却行动自如

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=313df6b9&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fsz_mmbiz_gif%2FRvq8Ow69CYWcWm1suywiaWMuDvsKKYx2Bu9a3qFkY5xHlcespjQ0wmbcT54ZLMaKOgz39nia0mFHOZKKkMJkSdp9NkPnjzp8oksiarC5f1C9yM%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dgif%26from%3Dappmsg)

许多机器人在这一关摔惨了，甚至直接退出比赛

这背后，就是智元搭载的生成式通用小脑引擎框架AGILE。

在这个强悍的小脑驱动下，灵犀X2在强化学习运动控制算法。

它不仅能在通过不规则障碍物时兼具速度与稳定，还能在多种复杂地形下实现自主或半自主的瞬间决策。

更绝的是，通过精准的参数辨识，智元显著缩小了虚拟仿真与现实之间的差距，确保了这套算法在比赛中拥有极强的鲁棒性。

这，正是具身AI大脑赋予机器人的真正「灵魂」！

**![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=0356db0c&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fsz_mmbiz_png%2FUicQ7HgWiaUb351381bTy5MO2IN89mV41M88GEiaCCibDxJoaQjYV6HfRtafnmEmfM3R1p0tmkHgBOVuXBD6UJKpsQ%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dpng%26from%3Dappmsg)**

**赛场即职场，场景赛狂揽6金**

如果你觉得机器人只是用来拿奖的，那就大错特错了。

这次运动会的场景赛板块，考核的可是实打实的社会作业能力——图书馆理书、消防应急灭火、酒店客房整理……这些人类要干的活，都是真的繁琐。

结果，在这个板块的12块金牌中，智元精灵G2直接豪取6金！

酒店、图书馆里的活儿有多难？

图书馆理书，要识别书籍、规划顺序、精准取放；酒店整理，要处理柔软、形态不固定的物品；消防灭火，要在陌生环境里完成感知、移动和操作。

在这些真实任务中，如果机器人看不懂环境、规划不了长任务，或者手上稍微失准，整套流程立刻卡住。

而且，真实工作也很少只有一个动作。

以图书馆理书为例，机器人要先找到目标书籍，判断书脊方向和抓取位置，再避开周围物体，把书送到正确位置。中间任何一步出现偏差，后续动作都得跟着调整。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=d9344fd8&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fsz_mmbiz_gif%2FRvq8Ow69CYUjZC094icHWX58throG4y3EptxicwFibQwldw1gDYKKVJX86l6rrViamKluzgR1OCw2FZ9a4ECjOxVLEIAfEnjDicG7ER595JM6GBM%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dgif%26from%3Dappmsg)

酒店整理同样麻烦，毛巾、床品等柔性物体形态随时变化，传统程序很难靠固定坐标解决。

消防灭火则把要求继续拉高，机器人要在开放环境中完成移动、识别、决策和操作，还要面对突发干扰。

这些项目，看起来没有跑跳翻滚那么炸裂，却更接近机器人真正进入社会后的工作日常。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=9839c93d&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fsz_mmbiz_gif%2FRvq8Ow69CYUm9ZN3v5duyudrtBgZ1QQ0nmxrvFd0QZSXXvp2nZEaOSFomJEB1dztSknJtdUZolckm94P8RzLtpLO4BZjlJRsVJ1qMibakQ4o%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dgif%26from%3Dappmsg)

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=9d0204d6&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fmmbiz_gif%2FRvq8Ow69CYWnibmmPiaE2jnjv4IIzODvY09My9PiaewKIMhuOBmz3Jvtx5LD9c8bmcJQkuv1dW5zm1PY5gRgsibE0YUApvumaljzl0gwvaZlRAQ%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dgif%26from%3Dappmsg)

对智元来说，这些题并不陌生。

参赛的精灵G2，早已进入龙旗科技、上汽等真实产线。

此前，8台G2在龙旗工厂连续6天覆盖整条平板质检工段，完成多媒体界面、音频、辐射杂散发射和耦合等多道检测，生产产品超过17500件，作业成功率达到99.99%。

它参加运动会之前，已经在工厂里上过班了。

能在这种环境中稳定工作，机器人才能积累真正有价值的「工龄」。这些真实部署经验，又会反过来提高它在陌生任务中的稳定性。

赛场由此成了一次高密度的商业化预演。

今天能整理酒店、归置图书、处理险情，明天对应的就是服务、公共空间和特种作业里的真实岗位。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=6568e90c&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fsz_mmbiz_png%2FUicQ7HgWiaUb3uEdSPKrwGNmZEOaaGyzVvZ8dTtE9jU1rFsda3llYbCZpmWfiazUYjWBLTGvlPpXucH8Q0lEUJN3Q%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dpng%26from%3Dappmsg)

**智元深厚的全栈技术**

**以及具身AI大脑**

这一切优异的成绩，归根结底源于智元深厚的全栈技术，而后者的核心灵魂，就在于「具身AI大脑」！

智元把自己的技术底座总结成四个字「三智一体」：一个可靠的本体，加上运动智能、交互智能、作业智能三层大脑。

四肢发达还得头脑灵活，能说会道还得干活利索，缺一不可。

这次比赛，恰好把三层大脑各考了一遍。

田径障碍赛，考的是运动智能。智元给灵犀X2装上了「真正的眼睛」，靠自研的AGILE生成式小脑引擎。

它让机器人能在多种地形下实现自主或半自主决策。不仅跑得快，而且走得稳。

在作业智能方面，智元依托自研的ViLLA具身基座大模型GO、世界模型GE和大规模分布式RW-RL构建了强大的智能系统。

这套AI能力有多硬，第三方榜单已经投过票——GE 2.0登顶具身领域权威榜单WorldArena全球第一！

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=2a8ef5a6&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fmmbiz_jpg%2FRvq8Ow69CYX9OKIPvUrSVnph023vbz1xicPwvfJtcRWl22RJxRce0mQyWUums6eFweK7iah4kx5KA4DPytYA82DjKEFJ2hsMy4hQGzcA8Os3w%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dwebp%26from%3Dappmsg)

这意味着机器人不是在执行死程序，而是能够自主感知、理解物理世界，在真实环境中闭环完成复杂任务，甚至具备跨本体、小样本的快速泛化能力！

另外，在交互智能层面，WITA-Omni Preview登顶了DailyOmni全模态理解榜单，在八项细分指标中六项第一。

它把看、听、说、动整合为一个连续过程，让机器人成为一个拥有在场感的交互伙伴。

更妙的是，这颗大脑会越用越聪明。

机器人在产线、在赛场干的每一件活，都会变成数据自动回流，喂给下一代模型。

智元把这叫「部署态数据飞轮」，干得越多，攒的数据越多，下一版就越强。

这也是为什么它敢让量产机直接上赛场：因为这些机器人本来就在真实世界里日夜训练，赛场只是它众多「工位」中新添的一个。

身体是载体，大脑才是胜负手。

这届运动会真正的冠军，是那颗跑在机器人体内、还在不断进化的具身AI大脑。

**![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=0356db0c&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fsz_mmbiz_png%2FUicQ7HgWiaUb351381bTy5MO2IN89mV41M88GEiaCCibDxJoaQjYV6HfRtafnmEmfM3R1p0tmkHgBOVuXBD6UJKpsQ%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dpng%26from%3Dappmsg)**

**双榜第一，含金量就在「量产」**

总之，这次智元机器人的金牌，含量超高。

这一次，2056台人形机器人会师北京「冰丝带」，51个赛项、1301场对决，除障碍赛外所有竞技项目都要求全自主完成。

就拿竞速项目来说，今年100米障碍赛50支队伍参赛，37支未能完赛，赛场淘汰率肉眼可见。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=a214f38d&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fsz_mmbiz_jpg%2FRvq8Ow69CYXZVF6ye8GeZy19dx2Sia1TVaUlDalen3foibapsy9XTyLDytjvTibZSVH8pCaF8ljFy8yGAoaE6c0SZTeE3GMWEZc0AicpuEOOfEY%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Djpeg%26from%3Dappmsg)

更加推高含金量的，就是智元用的是量产级。

原因很简单，定制样机可以围绕一个项目，把速度、结构和算法推到极限。

然而，量产机面对的约束多得多：成本要可控，结构要稳定，零部件要一致，还得经得起高强度连续运行。

所以，量产机的成绩更加意义重大：它验证的不只是实验室里的性能上限，还有产品一致性、可靠性和真实交付能力。

翻遍参赛名单，很多队伍会为比赛做特化——换更轻的外壳、上更贵的传感器、针对单一赛项调一版专用程序。

然而，这种赛场特供机，和现实应用却隔得很远。

在本场赛事上，智元派上场的，全部是量产机。

远征A3量产机上场比武术和舞蹈，精灵G2量产机上场做酒店整理和图书馆理书，灵犀X2量产机上场跑100米障碍赛，OmniHand量产版灵巧手上场做粉末称重和积木搭建。

其中，灵巧手专项8块金牌拿了7块，场景赛12块金牌拿了6块，竞技赛拿了5块金牌，田径赛也有金牌入账。

四类产品，四种形态，面对的是完全不同的任务。

最终都能站上领奖台，说明智元的优势已经跨过单点能力，进入平台化输出阶段！

**![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=0356db0c&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fsz_mmbiz_png%2FUicQ7HgWiaUb351381bTy5MO2IN89mV41M88GEiaCCibDxJoaQjYV6HfRtafnmEmfM3R1p0tmkHgBOVuXBD6UJKpsQ%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dpng%26from%3Dappmsg)**

**XYZ曲线，开始接近终点**

回到今年4月APC 2026大会上，智元创始人邓泰华首次提出的那个判断——

2026年，是部署态的元年。 

具身智能正式从「开发态」迈入「部署态」，从「能动」走向「会干」。

他为整个具身智能行业，画了一条坐标，即XYZ曲线。

X曲线是开发尝鲜期，机器人能动起来了，做表演、做展示、提供情绪价值。

Y曲线是部署成长期，机器人从「能动」变成「会干活」，开始创造真实生产力。

Z曲线是终局，智能涌现，机器人通过物理世界的「图灵测试」。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=1f71e851&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fmmbiz_png%2FRvq8Ow69CYXlnzjqQ1tWicM4QhWPzicXn28p8NiaTtfuYfsMasCRwLjPQyBShmsAc21iaUDJhG5CrXLWJFV5q4icyDasVFD3DfzzJHhC8UAGFJBU%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dpng%26from%3Dappmsg)

这场运动会看似仍是一场竞技，题目却已经明显向Y曲线靠拢。

同一批量产机器人，既能完成高动态竞技，也能处理酒店、图书馆、应急处置等真实任务。

同一套AI底座，能够跨本体、跨项目迁移。赛场验证的能力，已经在产线上常态化运行。

截至6月底，智元第15000台具身机器人已经下线。从万台量产，到真实部署，再到量产机双榜第一，几条原本分散的线开始合到一起。

本体、数据、模型、场景，由此形成一个闭环。

这也让智元成为行业首家、也是目前唯一实现部署态的企业。

比赛结束后，金牌会被放进展柜。

但这些量产机器人，还会继续回到工厂、酒店、图书馆和更多真实岗位上班。

赛场赢一次是成绩，真实世界每天都能赢，才是产业的分水岭。

entries.title: 奥特曼还是CEO，OpenAI已经姓Brockman了
entries.content:
原创 ASI启示录 2026-08-28 12:47 北京

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=1dbbb222&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fsz_mmbiz_jpg%2FRvq8Ow69CYX9D61860nxPZZzLkqUCFUoY8Zq6WWTExR95gexdE5rUhjzLft2PGObPPWulLKsOACNia7dau51Wia5XXf4d7CvguvNopbNTuprI%2F0%3Fwx_fmt%3Djpeg)

CEO还在台前，方向盘已经换人

### 

### **新智元报道**

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=9821b506&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fsz_mmbiz_png%2FRvq8Ow69CYWGxcbmnyYvqrSqhntcbPdelKBG0JLug4pEX8icjBSe5eib6PekswOSvrq8ybatQJRDr9Vib5WOKaUuibKfLb5qH3J4kEIYmC4NQJU%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dpng%26from%3Dappmsg)

现在，掌舵OpenAI的是Greg Brokckman。

奥特曼还是CEO，但日常运营的大权，落在二把手Brockman手里。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=b3f0ac0d&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fsz_mmbiz_png%2FRvq8Ow69CYVVwsQkeHJHHYE39icJUQq7VHWys7kCCzqMHpnBSJBARAXLSMKjPonk8hcpd0b3vqMC0hoFicOEBlkRMCtrEEbJJYqwVD8R21jQA%2F640%3Ffrom%3Dappmsg)

过去一年，OpenAI风云激荡。乱局之中，一人岿然不动，悄然积聚权柄。

吊诡的是，Brockman的头衔多年未变，一直是总裁兼联合创始人。

但他权势日盛：ChatGPT产品策略、Codex统一智能体平台、企业销售、go-to-market、算力业务，OpenAI除研究之外的所有核心条线，几乎都攥进了他一个人手里。

API和应用产品负责人Thibault Sottiaux把话挑明了，「到最后所有人都向Greg汇报」。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=6568e90c&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fsz_mmbiz_png%2FUicQ7HgWiaUb3uEdSPKrwGNmZEOaaGyzVvZ8dTtE9jU1rFsda3llYbCZpmWfiazUYjWBLTGvlPpXucH8Q0lEUJN3Q%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dpng%26from%3Dappmsg)

**OpenAI风云激荡，Brokckman独揽大权**

这一年，OpenAI堪称天崩开局。

先是官司缠身。

与联合创始人马斯克对簿公堂，一场审判鏖战数月，轰动一时。

又被苹果提起高调的商业机密诉讼。

到了7月，一个未发布模型在安全测试中越狱、入侵HuggingFace，OpenAI只能公开认错，舆论哗然。

而IPO大关当前，高管却接连离场。

全年都有人走：Sora负责人Bill Peebles、科学部门VP Kevin Weil、B2B应用CTO Srinivas Narayanan，一个月内全线出走。另有两人以健康原因告别：CMO Kate Rouch，以及AGI部署CEO Fidji Simo。Simo从4月开始休病假。

风暴没有停，但4月才是真正的分水岭

本月，4月动荡后被强压重担的CRO Denise Dresser，上任仅8个月便突然抽身；数日之后，曾多年担任COO、近几个月负责「特别项目」的Brad Lightcap也宣告离开，说要「去闯一番新天地」。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=79c65f8e&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fmmbiz_png%2FRvq8Ow69CYVD3O9kcomOcJHIkdLdgSOUYib7VBj9iaHOwGw5I8PLHcBqXiauVQyMRkMM0dAX8CJFwjoQRYNicaCeEPfCGMpoS31OgxblpaRErnc%2F640%3Ffrom%3Dappmsg)

律所SRFC合伙人Ross Carmel对The Verge直言，上市前有高管离职并不稀奇，「但所有人都挤在这么短的时间窗口里，这就不寻常了」。

8月17日，Brockman亲自上CNBC《Squawk Box》灭火。他说高管流动没什么反常：「不同时期，我们有不同的领导班子……我是常量，奥特曼也是常量。正因为这种韧性和多样性，我们才更强大。」

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=e8d4c757&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fmmbiz_png%2FRvq8Ow69CYU6gU1ugESpNytCwwMOypRIJ3aejnbPcibicRx9kUeoZ1FvC0SYP46ulmoHBxCiaFhzbrn7zkGv8Sbb8yvXRyzRrBzBqUJEQV0pVQ%2F640%3Ffrom%3Dappmsg)

9天后，Chris Malone离开。

此人管的是数据中心扩张，而算力正是OpenAI相对Anthropic最贵、也最想讲清楚的护城河。

据报道，基础设施改组后他不再直接向Brockman汇报，改向副总裁Sachin Katti汇报。这更像权力上收后的层级下移，而不是「每个时代自然换人」。Brockman8月17日的那句「不反常」，在8月26日已经需要再解释一轮。

这另一层现实好处：砍掉几份最贵的高管薪酬，让报表在上市前更好看。「对营收落后于Anthropic的OpenAI来说，你要么更盈利，要么离盈利更近。」

分析师甚至给出了时间表：9月底之前，OpenAI会在Brockman主导下推出某种消费级产品，好让他「证明自己配得上这个位置」。

变量走了一批又一批。牌桌上，只剩两个常量。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=6568e90c&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fsz_mmbiz_png%2FUicQ7HgWiaUb3uEdSPKrwGNmZEOaaGyzVvZ8dTtE9jU1rFsda3llYbCZpmWfiazUYjWBLTGvlPpXucH8Q0lEUJN3Q%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dpng%26from%3Dappmsg)

**牌桌上的两个人**

OpenAI的Brockman，如今只在奥特曼一人之下。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=72ed406d&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fsz_mmbiz_png%2FRvq8Ow69CYX9pv12aO8QrxJd42aGeCFFQQpwRjMLB0tIahuozGgXrA7mIa1gjfMJg9IhybMlx6COvhbuVqj0CMkuS8Zk2SXAn1qEzOxx6xk%2F640%3Ffrom%3Dappmsg)

在OpenAI之前，Brockman最知名的履历是拓展Stripe的业务，而在内部则以倡导公司的市场推广工作而闻名。

2015年12月，OpenAI以非营利实验室亮相。

当时，马斯克是最大早期出资人兼公开招牌，奥特曼当时仍是Y Combinator总裁、负责招募与对外叙事，Brockman从Stripe CTO离职、早期办公室就在他家客厅，Ilya从Google Brain过来，给实验室学术信誉。

2017年，彼时的OpenAI还只是一家标榜着「非营利」、「拯救人类」的纯粹研究机构。

但在那一年的个人日志里，下一句耐人寻味的话：「财务上，什么能让我赚到10亿美元？」

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=4808880a&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fmmbiz_png%2FRvq8Ow69CYWR6zRdcsgrYmQhFYHkM2ISA87a4WEpxNdicETKx3TboBXKUniaKxRZrsqsyIn7PKVocQZxU3p13dQjKpeYzThlcCGTVwXsib5STs%2F640%3Ffrom%3Dappmsg)

在2026年5月4日马斯克诉OpenAI案的庭审现场，一份震惊四座的法庭记录被公之于众。Brockman在庭审中确认，**他目前持有的OpenAI股份价值已接近300亿美元。**

更令人侧目的是，他承认自己从未向公司投入过哪怕一分钱现金。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=060e59bc&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fsz_mmbiz_png%2FRvq8Ow69CYWSuWjqiabbkDytKkQzdcBeUcqQc8yyVj3TicTBAYCQicEWP3jmQRslg3mCWYsiakQVSQnhGuXTfgricjcyhyO3G4659GmRzHI02tbQ%2F640%3Ffrom%3Dappmsg)

庭审中披露了一条隐藏极深的「财务纽带」：早在2017年，正是奥特曼将自己家族办公室中约1000万美元的权益，直接划给了Brockman，作为其在OpenAI「血汗与泪水」工作的补偿。

此外，Brockman还持有奥特曼其他相关初创公司的可观股份。

这一重磅炸弹，直接让马斯克暴跳如雷。马斯克的粉丝和支持者们更是狂轰滥炸，直指Brockman是「伪君子」。马斯克本人则暗讽其为**「全美国最耻辱的人之一」**。

抛开法庭上的唇枪舌剑不谈，这起诉讼向外界释放了一个极其明确的信号：**奥特曼与Brockman，在利益上早已深度绑定。**

**![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=0356db0c&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fsz_mmbiz_png%2FUicQ7HgWiaUb351381bTy5MO2IN89mV41M88GEiaCCibDxJoaQjYV6HfRtafnmEmfM3R1p0tmkHgBOVuXBD6UJKpsQ%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dpng%26from%3Dappmsg)**

**他也左右摇摆**

有意思的是，两人早年并非铁板一块。

在OpenAI早期的艰难岁月里，在关乎权力格局和技术路线的重大决策中，Brockman并非总是对奥特曼言听计从。

有时，他会站在首席科学家Ilya Sutskever这一边，对奥特曼那极度膨胀的商业野心表示担忧；但他同样忌惮强势的马斯克会彻底「碾压」奥特曼。

到了2017至2018年，关于OpenAI是否转营利、算力如何融资，几人爆发了激烈的控制权争执。

马斯克要求绝对控制权，否则就把OpenAI并入特斯拉。

Brockman对此坚决反对：「不该存在一个人对OpenAI拥有完全控制。」

最终，谈判破裂，马斯克在2018年离场。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=5bdeaf5b&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fsz_mmbiz_png%2FRvq8Ow69CYWWSrGyNa4pjc7cgmkDG4jxwm5VBn99VIodzUgdD2F9RKdu8ricZV7ddajzNAJOOTZrWu6kQFqck17veZT1Ao9orZVdcFKVyocU%2F640%3Ffrom%3Dappmsg)

随后，2019年OpenAI正式确立了「capped-profit」（有限营利）结构。而早在2017年那笔千万美元的家族办公室权益，早已在奥特曼和Brockman之间，写下了金钱与权力的双重契约。

在2019年OpenAI确立营利结构、奥特曼正式出任CEO之后，Brockman曾一度交出了大块的日常管理权。

但Brockman经常以创始人的身份，突然空降到各个项目里。

他会在最后一刻强行推翻早已定好的计划，加入自己的代码或功能。这种「冲进别人的项目制造混乱，再让其他高管（如CTO Mira Murati）去收场」的管理风格，让内部怨声载道，埋下了「OpenAI宫变」的导火线。

但不可否认的是，他的贡献同样巨大。

Brockman的一贯角色，是把OpenAI的研究变成能卖钱的东西。

2020年，他为GPT-3和开发者API欢呼：这是「OpenAI第一次拥有具备即时商业价值的通用AI系统，它真的有用」。

正是Brockman完成了OpenAI从「论文实验室」到「能开票赚钱的商家」的惊险一跃。

2022年他和奥特曼到盖茨家演示GPT-4生物题，2023年3月他主持GPT-4直播发布。

**![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=0356db0c&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fsz_mmbiz_png%2FUicQ7HgWiaUb351381bTy5MO2IN89mV41M88GEiaCCibDxJoaQjYV6HfRtafnmEmfM3R1p0tmkHgBOVuXBD6UJKpsQ%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dpng%26from%3Dappmsg)**

**真正的转折点**

**真正的分界线，在2023年11月17日。**

那天，Ilya联合董事会，以「对董事会不够坦诚」为由，突然罢免了奥特曼的CEO职务。而作为时任董事长的Brockman，竟然被完全蒙在鼓里，直接被移除了董事会。

那一刻，面临政治生涯的最大危机，Brockman没有丝毫犹豫。他在X上发文：「基于今天的消息，我辞职。」

他选择立刻声援奥特曼，转头就跟着他在酒店里筹划起新的AI公司。五天后，在微软的强势施压和几乎全体员工的罢工威胁下，原董事会土崩瓦解，奥特曼王者归来，Brockman并肩回归。

2024年8月5日，他公开表示：休到年底，创办九年第一次真正休息。

原计划约四个月，11月中旬提前回来，对内说正和奥特曼商量一个更偏技术难题的新角色。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=b39ed13f&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fsz_mmbiz_png%2FRvq8Ow69CYW0uEGuHULQ2uq5cnCGYZPJ9icbOgTMvnm5TvhZ0zZ310ht7ibHZcIrKtEeXWCmoesQibNM2heMLYzZWRA47lT2ju6jfo9NPrkynE%2F640%3Ffrom%3Dappmsg)

如今，当年的联合创始人所剩无几──

联合创始人里，马斯克走了，Ilya走了，Karpathy、舒尔曼走了，Murati也早已离开，而Wojciech Zaremba也不在OpenAI核心位置。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=3f01783c&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fsz_mmbiz_png%2FRvq8Ow69CYWGuCZzAz7bZ4cjYgKHFoUlfPojJWg19O64iakSeXIpicAnj8U9ENj0lB5Us3ZH9R5xSic94tBcJQqYK1QCL7lo0uvYrtVvXU1Nib0%2F640%3Ffrom%3Dappmsg)

能从实验室一路走到准备IPO还留在牌桌上的，只有奥特曼和Brockman。

entries.title: 10年前赌输的创业，被AI救活！以后人人都能改自己的App
entries.content:
ASI启示录 2026-08-28 12:47 北京

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=a870588c&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fsz_mmbiz_jpg%2FRvq8Ow69CYWwYrdsvW6JDtniaoCc8ibh70oMKZEz6pia8fF5xrT37uIHyv4pasmT5PnmWL5tCVl68vibialIxguVylr4MDqg9ibMgibjJPic4IXWbwM%2F0%3Fwx_fmt%3Djpeg)

### 

### **新智元报道**

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=9821b506&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fsz_mmbiz_png%2FRvq8Ow69CYWGxcbmnyYvqrSqhntcbPdelKBG0JLug4pEX8icjBSe5eib6PekswOSvrq8ybatQJRDr9Vib5WOKaUuibKfLb5qH3J4kEIYmC4NQJU%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dpng%26from%3Dappmsg)

我收藏的长文，全推到我的阅读器上。

每周扫一遍arXiv，跟我方向沾边的论文都留下，贴好标签。

我常看的网站抓下来老是乱码，给它单独写个解析器。

这是Cloudflare首席工程师Jeremy Morrell的「独家需求」，他手上的那个阅读App，一条也做不到。

他想要的是，这几句话说完，就有个机器人把对应的零碎代码挤出来，挂到软件预留好的扩展点上，然后自己跑起来。

做完还能顺手分享出去，谁想要谁拿走。

这，才是他心目中理想的软件样子：可扩展软件（Extensible Software）。

Morrell认为今天我们用的绝大多数Web软件，都是静态的。

这个静态不是指网页技术，而是说你改不动它的逻辑。

功能在发布那天就定稿了，只能用，不能改。

AI让这一切都变了。

人人都能改自己的App，不再是梦。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=0f15c4a3&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fsz_mmbiz_png%2FRvq8Ow69CYWLQf91soj2RYBywO0waU9aoPdI6spLCiapIqkObTWxictxKGbl4AJzQxPT11pB6ia5fLggW7yvAudGH5sEXzfDkibII8XqXB0Y6To%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dpng%26from%3Dappmsg)

用户说「加个我要的功能」，电脑当场加上，用户回一句「nice」。Morrell说这就是他想要的软件。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=6568e90c&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fsz_mmbiz_png%2FUicQ7HgWiaUb3uEdSPKrwGNmZEOaaGyzVvZ8dTtE9jU1rFsda3llYbCZpmWfiazUYjWBLTGvlPpXucH8Q0lEUJN3Q%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dpng%26from%3Dappmsg)

**为什么你心心念的那些功能**

**永远没人做出来**

因为，全世界只有你一个人想要。

开发者的时间和注意力有限，所以他们只做服务最大用户群的功能。

有时，就算他们想全做，也做不了。

界面复杂度有上限，每多加一个功能，都是在给不需要它的人添堵。

如果这个功能的受众只有几百人，它反而让剩下几百万人的产品变难用了。

这两条约束，就是过去二十年产品经理一直难以解开的死结。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=267360b6&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fsz_mmbiz_png%2FRvq8Ow69CYWZl0Ugzdk82gOnzexIUBUR3icbicWtOoibhmMV8c6arCDyaj6md0icqU5Qzuy25JDFyOfZV2MbK6cAA2VcQf2Kw9QIia5JUBD4kYvQ%2F640%3Ffrom%3Dappmsg)

地图软件的用户需求分布。左侧是所有人都在问的导航问题，右侧长尾是每个人各不相同的冷门需求。

你在某个App里想要的那个小功能，不是做不到，是做起来不划算。

过去一年，自从用户获得vibe coding能力之后，一切都变了。

做一个只服务一个人的工具，成本已经低到不值一提。

Y Combinator的Pete Koomen管这类东西叫小软件（Small Software）。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=dbfcc6d9&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fmmbiz_png%2FRvq8Ow69CYXHTN3UEAGLJJyVRWIlKApkbpPAnvjaAYiaagpn1xaMPwcyzTAfZ3VCjl9iaicdicd9X8RYLGicfrmDh1Gt84PNyd9Fa9fIAicc2RoEk%2F640%3Ffrom%3Dappmsg)

Y Combinator谈小软件：这类工具往往只服务一个人，或者一小撮人。

会计、医生、律师，还有另外几千种职业，都可以拥有自己趁手的「小软件」。

很显然，想让更多人用上智能体，别指望把他们都变成工程师。

该动的是软件。 

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=6568e90c&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fsz_mmbiz_png%2FUicQ7HgWiaUb3uEdSPKrwGNmZEOaaGyzVvZ8dTtE9jU1rFsda3llYbCZpmWfiazUYjWBLTGvlPpXucH8Q0lEUJN3Q%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dpng%26from%3Dappmsg)

**写扩展的成本归零了**

**收扩展的地方还没有**

代码好写了，问题跟着来了：写完往哪儿放。

今天不少Web产品留给用户的口子是webhook，门槛高得离谱：你得自己跑一整套独立服务，还得扛住投递环节冒出来的各种破事。

真正要让陌生代码在你的系统里跑起来，Morrell认为得过五道关。

第一关，钱。

假设有一百万个用户，每人都挂着自己那几行代码。要是给每人开一个容器，这笔账当场就算不下去。

Morrell给出的标准是：代码没被调用时，成本约等于零；调用一次，价格压到几分之一美分。

再加上编译、存文件、收日志，最后单台机器能塞下多少用户，全看内存开销一个指标。

第二关，冷启动。

用户代码卡在响应请求的关键路径上，等不了一分钟起容器，理想值是个位数毫秒。只跑定时任务或者事件回调的，可以放宽。

第三关，限额。

你永远猜不到用户会写出什么东西。Morrell讲了个他在Heroku听来的真事。

当年有份很火的入门教程，手把手教新手把自己的第一个程序部署到网上。教程里那个程序一共两行：一个死循环，不停地打印hello world。

一个应用凭空冒出来，出生第一秒就每秒吐几百万行日志，永不停止。

而跟着教程走的新手毫不知情，还在那边调出实时日志，指望屏幕上滚出点正常东西。

所以，CPU用多少、内存占多少、能往外发几个网络请求、每个请求多大、返回多少内容、一秒钟能写多少条日志，每一项都得卡死上限。

第四关，隔离，有两层。

崩溃、死循环、疯狂申请内存，不能影响到任何别的用户。恶意代码不能逃逸，也不能窥探别的租户，还得防住Spectre这类推测执行攻击。

第五关，代码要真能做事。什么都碰不到的代码，没有用。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=6568e90c&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fsz_mmbiz_png%2FUicQ7HgWiaUb3uEdSPKrwGNmZEOaaGyzVvZ8dTtE9jU1rFsda3llYbCZpmWfiazUYjWBLTGvlPpXucH8Q0lEUJN3Q%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dpng%26from%3Dappmsg)

**从给钥匙**

**到给一扇能推开的门**

怎么让不可信的代码干活，又不把家底交出去。

Morrell拆解了业内的三代解法。

第一代，直接给API密钥。

Morrell认为这种灵活性很危险。拿到密钥的代码，转手就能POST给第三方；就算它不偷，你的基础设施也随时能被拿去DoS别人。

第二代，加一个中转层（proxy）。

用户手上拿到的是一个不透明令牌，只对代理有意义；代理验完，换成真凭据再转发出去，顺带做白名单和限流。

这确实比裸奔强，但代价在维护上。你想把权限收窄到只允许一部分操作，就得在代理里写过滤逻辑，还得随着上游API演进一直改。

Morrell在文中贴了一段示例，那还只是「读一封已批准的邮件」这一个操作，代码就已经又长又难测。

而且这类逻辑几乎不可能想全。用户会干什么，你猜不到。

第三代，才是关键：能力（capability）。

不给钥匙，也不给地址，直接递过去一个现成的函数。比如「把那封已经批准的邮件取回来」，就这一个动作，别的什么也做不了。

用户的代码手上只有这几个函数。凭据从头到尾没进过它的地盘，就算拿到了数据，也没有通道送出去。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=1137e23e&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fmmbiz_png%2FRvq8Ow69CYWcCwWpuU1wBibNUoPia90HibTtWsVPJOmiaW72Da3uh4qPBZukhHtFnpOcnhibKFWn3pGMpCpS0XK9OLyiacq6PFP0ZpbFica5e2ksw0%2F640%3Ffrom%3Dappmsg)

前两行是平台自己的代码，钥匙握在这里。下面的函数是用户写的代码，它连钥匙长什么样都没见。

还有一个附带好处：把一份TypeScript写的能力定义丢给大模型，比甩一堆OpenAPI格式的JSON既省token又更准。

所以，真正的门槛，不是让AI写出代码，是决定这段代码能碰到什么。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=6568e90c&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fsz_mmbiz_png%2FUicQ7HgWiaUb3uEdSPKrwGNmZEOaaGyzVvZ8dTtE9jU1rFsda3llYbCZpmWfiazUYjWBLTGvlPpXucH8Q0lEUJN3Q%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dpng%26from%3Dappmsg)

**四条路**

**没有一条是免费的**

能不能写扩展，二十年前就有答案了。大模型改变的是谁能写。

Morrell列了四条路：

最轻的一档是嵌入式解释器：Lua、QuickJS这类，或者干脆自己造一个。

再往上是V8 Isolates。

Google往V8的安全加固里砸了海量的钱和人，直接用就省掉了自己造轮子。

这条路上有Cloudflare的Dynamic Workers、Node的isolated-vm、Rivet的secure-exec。

第三档是MicroVM。

它把完整虚拟机里那些USB、显卡、磁盘的模拟全砍掉，只留骨架，隔离最硬、能跑二进制、有完整POSIX，代价是开销明显更大。

Firecracker、libkrun都在这一档。

第四档是WASM加WASI。

WebAssembly一开始就是一张白纸，连发HTTP请求、读环境变量的模块都没有，权限全靠宿主显式授予。

从安全角度看这是最漂亮的起点，代价是工具链复杂得多。

这四条不是互相替代。

WASM可以跑在V8 Isolates里，也可以跑在MicroVM里。哪怕你拿V8 Isolates或WASM做隔离边界，MicroVM在编译打包、测试扩展这些环节照样有用。

这套东西能不能跑，Morrell自己先试了一把。他把自己的静态博客改造成一个Demo，自嘲是「世界上最小的vibe coding平台」。

本质是个可定制的抓取器：给一个URL，它抓回内容，连同几个预先授予的工具一起交给用户代码，你可以直接改源码然后运行。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=6568e90c&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fsz_mmbiz_png%2FUicQ7HgWiaUb3uEdSPKrwGNmZEOaaGyzVvZ8dTtE9jU1rFsda3llYbCZpmWfiazUYjWBLTGvlPpXucH8Q0lEUJN3Q%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dpng%26from%3Dappmsg)

**10年前赌输的想法**

**被AI救活了**

十年前，现为Cloudflare Workers技术负责人的Kenton Varda曾做过一个叫Sandstorm.io的创业项目。

它的主张在当年听着有点怪：你打开的每一份文档，都跑在属于它自己的沙箱实例里；程序拿不到任何你没有亲手递过去的东西。不发钥匙，只发能力。

这个项目没做起来。

Varda后来复盘失败原因：没人有那个耐心，把软件一个一个手工打包成那副样子。

十年过去。2026年8月5日，Cloudflare把这套东西以Apache 2.0协议重新开源，名字叫Cloudflare OS。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=7bdaac6f&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fmmbiz_png%2FRvq8Ow69CYUyVTU08tQ68dVlj2GRP6ZrU55Egh6CXaZhWWCcT10uYiatsreP7D1XW3pib9B3GAghKyKfklDRHiazUfriafteezGBl8nICiaib4lAY%2F640%3Ffrom%3Dappmsg)

Cloudflare OS，2026年8月5日以Apache 2.0协议开源。Sandstorm.io十年前赌的那件事，换了个壳回来了。

Varda当天在X上写：这差不多是我那个秘密十年大计的集大成。

当年他缺的那份耐心，AI补上了。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=6568e90c&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fsz_mmbiz_png%2FUicQ7HgWiaUb3uEdSPKrwGNmZEOaaGyzVvZ8dTtE9jU1rFsda3llYbCZpmWfiazUYjWBLTGvlPpXucH8Q0lEUJN3Q%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dpng%26from%3Dappmsg)

**软件真的要变软了**

OpenAI在《Codex as a Platform》里开源了Codex的智能体框架，讲的几乎是同一件事：

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=daacc10e&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fsz_mmbiz_png%2FRvq8Ow69CYXCCNVjqicxZCgmIkjk6HJyK8FkIUtqOEUatXJxhxe3PFKny9egeJWTOz64ID6nZc6OYWRJJiaFVC3tumHuWQ6kpXfLlKSfz7J7U%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dpng%26from%3Dappmsg)

与其让每个团队都把活儿搬进一个通用编码助手，不如把智能体嵌进他们本来就在用的软件里。

工程流程、运维仪表盘、安全调查、客服控制台，每一样都能装。

分工也划得清楚：界面、业务上下文、工具和审批边界归应用方，智能体循环和沙箱执行归框架。

他们做的示例应用Relay，把一个智能体放在货运仪表盘旁边，接上应用自己的MCP工具，改签之前必须人工批准。

![](https://wechat2rss.bestblogs.dev/img-proxy/?k=60dd0e10&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmmbiz.qpic.cn%2Fmmbiz_png%2FRvq8Ow69CYWETYy88ibMlXNZfF5azB3CJsaGKM3iaY2MibIFH8UNGnTX3icDDhq9Oz3DsbraNtsILUia6uV2vz6VEL9DrVv4V26fvdibwkbh0rneI%2F640%3Fwx_fmt%3Dpng%26from%3Dappmsg)

现在不少公司在鼓励员工自己vibe coding做工具，方向对，麻烦在后面。

几百上千个这样的应用，谁来维护？怎么保证它只拿到该拿的那部分数据？访问令牌的权限范围谁定，谁来轮转？会不会顺手把客户信息写进第三方日志？GDPR怎么办？

Morrell给的答案是：给他们一个根本没有令牌可以泄露的地方去部署，数据访问交给平台团队统一兜住合规。

这件事真要成，产品经理的活儿就变了。

你不必覆盖所有长尾需求，但你必须设计稳定的扩展点、能力接口，还有对兼容性的长期承诺。厂商不主动开这个口子，用户一点也扩不动。

Morrell在平台这行干了快十年，他没把话说得很轻松：平台难设计，难运维，难调试。对外暴露API，意味着大量的前期思考和长期支持。

但他还是那两个字：值得。

因为你会被用户的创造力吓一跳，他们做出来的东西，是你从没设想过、甚至以为不可能的。

以后判断一个App好不好，可能要多问一句：它允许你改多少。

entries.title: A third of new webpages written with AI
entries.content:
[![](https://flowingdata.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/signs_of_ai_authorship_are_less_common_in_edu_and_gov_domains-750x648.png)](https://flowingdata.com/2026/08/28/a-third-of-new-webpages-written-with-ai/)

It is trivial to generate bodies of text on infinite topics, so of course the web is filled with the stuff. [Pew Research tried to estimate how much](https://www.pewresearch.org/data-labs/2026/08/20/how-much-of-the-internet-is-written-with-ai/).

> To explore this question, we used the [Common Crawl](https://commoncrawl.org/) web archive to collect almost half a million English-language webpages from the past five years – starting a couple of years before the release of ChatGPT. We then ran the text of those pages through an AI detection tool called [Open Pangram](https://www.pangram.com/blog/introducing-open-pangram) to see how many of them were likely written or substantially edited by AI.

In a random sample, 9% of English language webpages were marked as having signs AI authorship. When looking at only pages that went live after the release of ChatGPT, they found a much a higher rate of 1 in 3.

Caveats considered, such as the accuracy and false positives with Open Pangram, the upward trends are clear. I am not sure how I feel about this, but I do not like that the em dash and Oxford comma are now a mark of AI usage.

**Tags:** [Internet](https://flowingdata.com/tag/internet/), [Pew Research](https://flowingdata.com/tag/pew-research/), [writing](https://flowingdata.com/tag/writing/)
