entries.title: Russian APT BlueDelta Uses HOOKEDGE to Target Defense and Diplomatic Organizations
entries.content:
## ****BlueDelta (APT28) uses webhook.site and Microsoft Edge to hide HOOKEDGE espionage traffic targeting European governments.****

[Recorded Future’s Insikt Group documented](https://www.recordedfuture.com/research/bluedelta-targets-with-hookedge) a campaign by [BlueDelta](https://securityaffairs.com/tag/bluedelta), the Russian GRU-linked group that overlaps with the [group APT28](https://securityaffairs.com/tag/apt28), running an entire espionage operation against European government targets using webhook.site, a service built for developers to test HTTP requests, as its command-and-control backbone.

The campaign ran from late September 2025 through early April 2026, targeting government and diplomatic organizations in Romania, Spain, and Türkiye.

*“The campaigns delivered a lightweight Windows batch-script backdoor, dubbed “HOOKEDGE,” via macro-enabled Microsoft Word documents using diplomatic-themed lures, including material impersonating Spain’s Ministry of the Presidency, Justice and Relations with the Cortes, created shortly after a September 2025 meeting between Spanish and Moldovan officials.” states the [report](https://www.recordedfuture.com/research/bluedelta-targets-with-hookedge) by Insikt Group.*

*“Insikt Group assesses with moderate confidence that this activity was conducted by BlueDelta (which overlaps with APT28, Fancy Bear, and Forest Blizzard), a Russian state-sponsored threat group attributed to the Main Directorate of the General Staff of the Armed Forces of the Russian Federation (GRU).”*

The attackers used a fairly old-school trick: macro-enabled Word documents. One of them looked like a real meeting agenda from Spain’s Ministry of the Presidency and appeared shortly after an actual meeting between Spanish and Moldovan officials. The timing was interesting because it came just before Moldova’s September 2025 parliamentary elections. The document looked credible enough to make the phishing attempt believable.

[![](https://i0.wp.com/securityaffairs.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image-84.png?resize=1024%2C485&ssl=1)](https://i0.wp.com/securityaffairs.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image-84.png?ssl=1)

The backdoor, called HOOKEDGE, is surprisingly simple. It uses a Windows batch script and relies on two webhooks. One receives commands, while the other sends the stolen data back to the attackers. Every 30 minutes, a scheduled task downloads a command file through Microsoft Edge, runs it and sends the results to another endpoint. The malware uses Edge to make the traffic look like normal web activity, making it harder for security tools to spot.

That reliance on a real browser for both tasking and exfiltration is the cleverest part of the whole design.

“A notable aspect of HOOKEDGE is its use of `msedge.exe` for both tasking and exfiltration. By generating network traffic through a legitimate web browser rather than a commonly abused LotL binary (LOLBin) or a custom binary, the malware blends its communications with normal enterprise browsing activity.” continues the report.

Recorded Future explains, and that’s really the entire evasion strategy in one sentence: don’t build something exotic, just make your traffic look exactly like an employee checking a website.

BlueDelta didn’t build HOOKEDGE from scratch either. It shares deep code and structural overlap with HEADLACE, a backdoor the same group used years earlier, right down to identical JavaScript variable names and the same base64 encoding scheme for automated downloads.

“HOOKEDGE’s code and structural design have significant overlap with [HEADLACE](https://securityaffairs.com/tag/headlace-malware), a backdoor used by BlueDelta in [previous campaigns](https://www.recordedfuture.com/research/grus-bluedelta-targets-key-networks-in-europe-with-multi-phase-espionage-camp).” states the report.

[![](https://i0.wp.com/securityaffairs.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image-83.png?resize=1024%2C671&ssl=1)](https://i0.wp.com/securityaffairs.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/image-83.png?ssl=1)

Recorded Future assesses with moderate confidence that HOOKEDGE is a direct evolutionary successor, maintained by the same operators rather than a fresh tool built by a different team, which fits BlueDelta’s long-documented habit of refining working tradecraft instead of reinventing it.

The operation also included a triage mechanism worth understanding on its own. Once a victim showed signs of being worth deeper attention, active communication with the initial webhook endpoints, BlueDelta deployed a second HOOKEDGE payload configured to check in every five minutes instead of thirty, giving operators much faster interactive control over higher-value targets. That two-tier setup also solved a practical infrastructure problem: webhook.site’s free tier caps out at 100 requests per endpoint, so spreading routine and high-priority tasking across separate endpoints kept any single one from getting exhausted mid-operation.

BlueDelta kept tuning the operation continuously rather than treating it as a finished product. Beaconing intervals stretched from 30 minutes to 61, deliberately timed to slip past sandbox environments that typically only watch a sample’s behavior for an hour. The group added canary tracking pixels named things like mailopened.jpg and docopened.jpg to monitor exactly when a phishing email got opened versus when the document itself got opened versus when macros actually executed, essentially building analytics for their own phishing funnel.

*“The malicious document also contains a hidden image referencing a remote webhook URL: hxxp://webhook[.]site/62114596-33f5-47fb-9012-0223529e5a13/docopened[.]jpg. This serves as a document-open “canary,” alerting BlueDelta operators when a victim opens the lure. Later variants used the filename `doc.jpg` in place of `docopened.jpg`.” states Insik. “Insikt Group also identified webhooks using the filename `mailopened.jpg`, indicating that BlueDelta likely used a similar canary mechanism to monitor when recipients opened phishing emails, providing operators with visibility into campaign delivery success before any payload execution.”*

That kind of detailed tracking of what victims do would look very familiar to a marketing team. The difference is that here the targets are victims, not customers.

For defenders, the useful indicators are quite clear. Block macros in documents downloaded from the internet, monitor scheduled tasks that launch scripts from user-writable folders, and flag Microsoft Edge running in headless mode or making automated connections to file-sharing and webhook services that the organization does not normally use. You don’t need sophisticated tools to spot these behaviors. Even a well-configured monitoring system should be able to detect them early. The worrying part is that a persistent, state-backed group can still rely on a small set of behaviors that defenders can identify and block.

For defenders, the actionable pieces here are concrete rather than abstract. Block macro execution from documents that arrived over the internet, watch for scheduled tasks spawning script interpreters from user-writable folders, and specifically flag Microsoft Edge running in headless mode or making automated requests to file-hosting and webhook services your organization doesn’t actually use for anything legitimate. None of this requires exotic tooling to catch, which is oddly reassuring: a threat group this persistent and state-backed is still, at its core, relying on the same handful of detectable behaviors that a properly configured monitoring setup would catch on day one.

*“BlueDelta is likely to continue conducting initial access campaigns against European government and diplomatic organizations in support of Russian intelligence collection. Given the enduring strategic importance of European governance, NATO-related affairs, and diplomatic engagement with former Soviet republics, the intelligence requirements driving this activity are unlikely to diminish in the near term.” concludes the report.*

entries.title: Microsoft preps this year's Windows 11 feature tweaks: 26H2 hits Release Preview
entries.content: Microsoft has dropped Windows 11 26H2 into the Windows Insider Release Preview Channel and released August's preview update. Windows 11 26H2 shares the same servicing branch as Windows 11 24H2 and 25H2, and many of the tweaks and updates that users are looking forward to have already appeared in the monthly Windows updates. The latest, the August Preview Update, includes such modifications as the long-awaited movable taskbar, more Start Menu customization, and the ability to drop web and Microsoft Store suggestions from local results in Windows Search. The update will turn up via an enablement package – a relatively small piece of code that switches on functionality already downloaded, but currently dormant. "Think of it as a switch rather than a full operating system replacement," Microsoft wrote. It's considerably more compact than a multi-gigabyte full download and reinstall of an operating system. Resetting the support clock The shared codebase and shared updates – Windows 11 26H2 will share the same release note KB identifiers as 25H2 and 24H2 – might have some users wondering about the point. One answer is support. For example, support for the Home and Pro editions of Windows 11 24H2 ends on October 13, 2026. Windows 11 26H2 resets this clock, with 24 months of support for Home and Pro versions, and 36 months for Enterprise and Education editions. Enterprises will still need to validate the new release. The servicing branch is the same, and if something works with Windows 11 25H2 and 24H2, it should work with Windows 11 26H2. However, Microsoft still recommends "testing with devices running recent versions of Windows 11 to confirm compatibility with your apps, policies, and infrastructure." Some organizations will have already done this, while others will have waited until the Release Preview milestone was reached. Microsoft took careful aim at its foot when it skipped the Release Preview stage and released the infamous document-destroying Windows 10 October 2018 update. It has been considerably more cautious in the years since. The move to Release Preview was accompanied by the August Preview Update, which included a raft of improvements, but was also greeted with dismay by some users complaining of problems with cursors and black desktop backgrounds following the installation. As far as Microsoft is concerned, it is not currently aware of any issues with the update. ®

entries.title: The surprising science behind Japan’s vending machine obsession
entries.content:
Japan is [synonymous with vending machines](https://japanreportage.com/2025/12/15/how-japan-became-the-world-capital-of-vending-machines/). The island-nation has vending machines for [everything](https://en.japantravel.com/article/only-in-japan-vending-machines-that-go-way-beyond-drinks/71451): fresh flowers, [bowls of hot ramen](https://www.wa-mare.com/en/column/492/), edible grasshoppers, [umbrellas](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/life-style/travel/destinations/guess-the-place-it-has-vending-machines-selling-everything-from-eggs-to-umbrellas/articleshow/128191490.cms). Want a fresh farm egg or flower bouquet? There’s a vending machine for that!

Japan is home to [over 2.6 million](https://japan-dev.com/blog/how-many-vending-machines-in-japan) vending machines: meaning that with approximately [122 million residents](https://www.worldometers.info/world-population/japan-population/), there’s approximately one vending machine for every 45 to 50 people.

But it turns out these contraptions of convenience had quite a long history before they became popular in Japan. It’s a story that left us wondering: Just how did vending machines become so ubiquitous in this Asian country, and what’s the [science](https://www.popsci.com/category/science/) behind how they work?

To get some answers, *Popular Science* turned to [David Widjaja](https://www.linkedin.com/in/david-adi-widjaja-b591902/), former vending machine employee and current owner of [Japantogo LLC](https://japanasiatrade.com/), an Ishikawa-based exporter of Japanese vending machines, to give us the inside scoop.

## A brief history of vending machines

Famous Greek engineer and inventor [Hero of Alexandria](https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Heron/) created the [world’s first known vending machine](https://historyfacts.com/science-industry/fact/the-first-known-vending-machine-dispensed-holy-water/) in ancient Egypt during the first century AD. Hero utilized the powers of physics to dispense holy waters in temples. Hero’s dispenser used a simple counterweight lever system (picture the [scales of justice](https://macioleklawgroup.com/the-scales-of-justice/), with two hanging pans held by a horizontal beam that adjusts its position, depending on which pan is heavier). When someone dropped a coin into the contraption, the coin would land on one of the scale’s pans. The weight of the coin would then trigger a valve and let out a flow of holy water.

![Engraving depicting an ancient penny-in-the-slot vending machine.](https://www.popsci.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/hero-of-alexandria-vending-machine.jpg?strip=all&quality=85)

Famous Greek engineer and inventor Hero of Alexandria created the world’s first known vending machine in ancient Egypt to dispense holy water. *Image: Universal History Archive / Contributor / Getty Images /*  Universal History Archive

Despite its ingenuity, the concept of vending dispensers pretty much disappeared until the late 19th century. That’s when coin-operated [machines](https://www.popsci.com/category/technology/) [filled with postcards](https://www.ukvending.co.uk/info/what-did-the-earliest-vending-machines-sell?srsltid=AfmBOopBTqy5_nKaQKhh7GgHtqt-wmjKKR6wh1Wsmp8h-TTCEKgOusXk), envelopes, and notepaper began popping up on railway platforms throughout London for travelers on-the-go.

Soon, the device made its way across the pond. By 1888, the Thomas Adams Gum Company was placing [vending machines stocked with Tutti-Frutti chewing gum](https://historictownsofamerica.com/first-vending-machine) all along New York City’s transit lines. Before long, vending machines offered everything from cartons of [milk](https://www.popsci.com/health/is-raw-milk-safe/) to refrigerated [sandwiches](https://www.popsci.com/diy/y-cut-sandwich/).

Still, it wasn’t until [after World War II](http://youtube.com/watch?v=W-OyXqZlOso&t=21) that [vending machines](https://www.popsci.com/technology/restaurants-vending-machines-pandemic/) became a staple of Japanese culture. It happened during the country’s rapid postwar economic recovery.

“They’re very convenient,” says Widjaja. “Japanese people are often in a rush, and we want something on the go. If you go into the store, it can cost you four or five minutes of waiting.” With vending machines, you can get what you need immediately.

## How do vending machines work?

Vending machines rely on an [embedded computer system](https://dedicatedcomputing.com/embedded-computing-systems-101/), which is a specialized computer system designed for a specific use. In this case, the embedded computer consists of a microcontroller (a tiny, self-contained computer), sensors, and actuators (the gear motors and pusher tracks that open access hatches and get that soda to fall).

“Actually, vending machines are simple,” says Widjaja. The microcontroller acts as the machine’s “brain.” It receives user input (e.g. when you push your numbered selection), validates payment, and sends commands to the dispensing motors—the rotary power sources for each individual item.

## Related 'Ask Us Anything' Stories

[How do garbage trucks work?](https://www.popsci.com/science/how-garbage-trucks-work/)

[4 sunscreen myths too many people still get wrong](https://www.popsci.com/science/sunscreen-myths-podcast/)

[No, cruise ships aren’t floating petri dishes](https://www.popsci.com/science/what-diseases-on-cruise-ships/)

[Airplane seats really are getting smaller](https://www.popsci.com/science/airplane-seats-smaller-podcast/)

[Why you never forget how to ride a bike](https://www.popsci.com/science/why-never-forget-how-ride-bike/)

[It’s illegal to pump your own gas in New Jersey. But why?](https://www.popsci.com/environment/why-cant-pump-gas-new-jersey/)

[Why are airplanes so cold? It’s for your health.](https://www.popsci.com/science/why-planes-are-cold/)

### Payment validation

Once you put coins or paper money into a vending machine, the machine uses electromagnetic sensors to verify that the payment is legit. These sensors figure out which kinds of coins are inserted—and whether or not they’re authentic—by using electric and magnetic fields to determine a coin’s metal makeup. Basically, each metal alloy (e.g. nickel, iron, etc) produces a specific effect on the magnetic field.

For example, when cheap iron passes through the machine’s magnetic lines it becomes [temporarily magnetized](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LOi2AzSjkC8). On the other hand, pure aluminum can pass through these same magnetic lines with little effect. The machine’s microcontroller will then instantly compare these results against a pre-programmed database of real coins, determining  whether the coin inserted is real or fake.

At the same time, [optical sensors](https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/engineering/optical-sensors) measure the coin’s diameter, thickness, and speed. When a coin rolls down the vending machine’s chute, it casts a shadow on a light sensor. The microcontroller times exactly how long the light remains blocked. This allows it to calculate the coin’s precise diameter. Another light sensor measures how fast the coin is traveling, which helps the microcontroller confirm if it is moving abnormally fast or slow. If it’s one or the other, the coin is likely fake. The machine will then reject it.

For paper money, optical sensors use infrared and [UV light sensors](https://www.digikey.be/nl/articles/light-sensors-an-overview?srsltid=AfmBOoqcNv-Fh88Jlk3tl1GZou-m8IjbsM9rghkDo3rtbvao9QBt_Iab) to read hidden security markings and magnetic ink (banknotes are printed with special magnetic inks containing iron oxide).

If you’re using a credit card, the machine will send encrypted data through an attached [telemetry gateway device](https://www.delta-telemetry.com/products/model-2355-m16-telemetry-gateway/)—a hardware unit that collects data from the machine’s sensors—straight to a banking network. This allows the microcontroller to instantly verify if your payment is legitimate.

### Dispensing

After your payment is accepted and you’ve punched in the code for your desired soda or bag of chips, the microcontroller switches modes. This tiny brain then sends a signal to the [dispensing motor](https://patents.google.com/patent/US20040104239A1/en) assigned to the object that you’re purchasing.

Some machines use [spiral coils](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=isO3T3lLUMA&t=8s) that rotate 360 degrees and push a bag forward until it tips over the edge of the shelf. Others use robotic elevator arms or picker mechanisms that rise to a specific shelf, secure a drink, and gently lower it to prevent it from exploding.

There are also machines that utilize a traditional [gravity and drop system](https://drainboss.co.uk/glossary/gravity-system/), in which the selected product simply slides off a slanted shelf and falls directly into the retrieval bin.

In Japan, some vending machines even dispense bowls of hot ramen. *Video: Ramen Noodles Vending Machine in Tokyo, [TabiEats](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2-AKGzd-ywc)*

## How Japanese vending machines differ

Many vending machines also include small refrigeration units to keep things cold, or internal built-in microwaves and instant heaters (long, narrow internal pipes that heat up to 2,000 Watts within seconds) for warm drinks like coffee and tea.

However, dual-temperature machines that disperse both hot *and* cold products from the same unit are rare in the United States. That’s not the case in Japan, where Widjaja says vending machines are all about efficiency. “You can sell cold drinks during summer, and hot coffee during winter, all from one machine.”

These specialized units feature two separate, heavily insulated zones: one for hot beverages and one for cold beverages. Many modern dual-temperature vending machines also feature an innovative [heat-pump system](https://nachhaltigwirtschaften.at/en/news/2026/20260219-innovative-heat-pumps.php)—one that recycles the thermal energy generated from the machine’s cooler side and pipes it into its warm section. This helps to significantly reduce the machine’s overall energy consumption.

Because Japan is [prone to natural disasters](https://edition.cnn.com/2026/07/29/asia/japan-earthquake-kumamoto-ring-of-fire-intl-hnk), many of its vending machines are also designed to be “earthquake proof.” Their heavy parts, such as thick metal bases and compressor pumps that are actively circulating refrigeration gases to keep products cold, are built into the machine’s lower portion.

“We call this area the ‘basement,’” says Widjaja. The bottom-lying weight helps to steady the machines in earthquake zones. “In Japan, everything is about safety.”

Another feature: [free-dispense activation](https://www.businessinsider.com/japan-vending-machines-unlock-earthquake-give-free-food-disaster-2023-6). “We call it ‘free vending,’” says Widjaja. Say there’s a large earthquake in Tokyo. These machines may have built-in sensors that detect heavy shaking, or are programmed to receive signals from local city authorities. In either case, “a router inside automatically switches to ‘free mode.’ The machine will then disperse free drinks so that everyone can have a beverage.”

Although the number of vending machines in Japan [has recently been decreasing](https://www.japantimes.co.jp/business/2026/03/12/companies/declining-vending-machines/), in a country with [very low crime](https://www.facebook.com/reel/1716672676332824) and [millions of pedestrians on foot](https://citychangers.org/tokyos-pedestrian-paradises/) they still make sense.

“Japanese people like a lot of options,” says Widjaja. “Vending machines have these options, and you don’t have to wait in line!”

entries.title: Apple announces price increase for Apple TV and Apple One subscriptions
entries.content:
![](https://9to5mac.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/6/2026/05/apple-tv-sunset-mountains.jpg?quality=82&strip=all&w=1600)

Just [weeks after announcing](https://9to5mac.com/2026/07/17/apple-raises-prices-for-apple-music-and-apple-one-subscriptions/) price increases for Apple Music, Apple today announced that Apple TV is also getting more expensive. The Individual tier of Apple One is also getting more expensive.

entries.title: Apple TV acquires breakout British hit comedy for global streaming
entries.content:
![](https://9to5mac.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/6/2026/08/apple-tv-small-prophets.jpg?quality=82&strip=all&w=1600)

[Apple TV](https://tinyurl.com/getappletvplus) has picked up a new comedy series, *Small Prophets*, for its streaming service in an atypical fashion for the streamer. Rather than commission the project upfront, Apple has bought out the worldwide rights for the series a few months after the show debuted in the UK to record ratings.

*Small Prophets* was the biggest new scripted series launch for the BBC this year, and Apple will be hoping to replicate its success around the world. It streams on Apple TV starting October 7.

## This Ryobi cordless circular saw is 48% off

A circular saw is a necessary tool for most DIY woodworking and repair projects. You can use it to cut materials like plywood and two by fours. Having a portable circular saw is especially useful if you don’t have a table saw because you can use it to make long, straight cuts.

The [Ryobi 18-volt 7 ¼-inch circular saw](https://zdcs.link/QGjjpV?pageview_type=RSS&template=content&module=content_body&element=offer&item=text-link&element_label=Ryobi%2018-volt%207%20%C2%BC-inch%20circular%20saw&object_type=content&short_url=QGjjpV&u=https%3A%2F%2Flifehacker.com%2Ffeed%2Frss "open in a new window") is on sale for $139, 48% off its regular price. The saw comes with an 18-volt, 4-amp-hour battery. This saw has an attachment port for a shop vac or dust collection system, which can be used to control dust for safety as well as an easier cleanup.

## This Ryobi angle grinder is 60% off

An angle grinder can be used for cutting or grinding metal for DIY projects; you can use it to shape hardware or to cut off the ends of screws or nails that stick through your material. For any DIY projects that involve metalworking, an angle grinder is an essential tool.

The [Ryobi 18-volt angle grinder](https://zdcs.link/z7GG2E?pageview_type=RSS&template=content&module=content_body&element=offer&item=text-link&element_label=Ryobi%2018-volt%20angle%20grinder&object_type=content&short_url=z7GG2E&u=https%3A%2F%2Flifehacker.com%2Ffeed%2Frss "open in a new window") is now $99, 60% off its regular price. It comes with an 18-volt, 4-amp-hour battery. This grinder can make up to 210 cuts per charge on one battery so you’ll be able to get a lot done on a single charge. I use an angle grinder to nip off the ends of screws if they go too far through my joints and poke out.

## This Ryobi oscillating multitool is 60% off

An oscillating multitool is the most versatile tool in your cordless tool set; you can use it for cutting wood, PVC, metal, drywall, and more. You can get a variety of blades for cutting different materials and you can also swap out attachments for sanding and polishing.

The [Ryobi 18-volt oscillating multitool](https://zdcs.link/9w00qR?pageview_type=RSS&template=content&module=content_body&element=offer&item=text-link&element_label=Ryobi%2018-volt%20oscillating%20multitool&object_type=content&short_url=9w00qR&u=https%3A%2F%2Flifehacker.com%2Ffeed%2Frss "open in a new window") is currently $99, 60% off its usual price. It comes with an 18-volt, 4-amp-hour battery, a plunge-cut blade, a flush-cut blade, and a sanding attachment. You can adjust the speed of the oscillating tool for the specific project you’re working on. I like to use the sanding attachment when I’m refinishing furniture—it can get into tight spaces more easily than a larger tool.

## This Ryobi driver set is 69% off

A good quality cordless driver is an essential component of a DIY kit—you’ll need it for driving screws or drilling holes. For anything from fence repair to hanging a flat screen TV, a driver will be indispensable.

The [Ryobi 18-volt ¼-inch driver tool](https://zdcs.link/92ppP1?pageview_type=RSS&template=content&module=content_body&element=offer&item=text-link&element_label=Ryobi%2018-volt%20%C2%BC-inch%20driver%20tool&object_type=content&short_url=92ppP1&u=https%3A%2F%2Flifehacker.com%2Ffeed%2Frss "open in a new window") is on sale for $49.97, 69% off its typical price. This tool comes with an 18-volt battery and a charger. This is a good tool for a beginner DIY kit or for a home maintenance tool set. Because of its light weight design, it isn’t as powerful as an impact driver, so it isn’t recommended for heavier and denser materials like hardwoods or plaster.

entries.title: BotBase for Operators: A clearer path to joining Cloudflare's directory of bots and agents
entries.content:
Last month, on our second Content Independence Day, we announced [a couple of features](https://blog.cloudflare.com/content-independence-day-ai-options/) designed to give website owners more visibility and control over automated traffic: [BotBase](https://developers.cloudflare.com/bots/botbase/) added a searchable directory of known bots to the Cloudflare dashboard, while [Business Insights](https://blog.cloudflare.com/attribution-business-insights/) helped owners understand how crawlers interact with their content. We know that the ecosystem of bots is vast, making it all the more important for site owners to be able to manage bot traffic sustainably.

But this ecosystem goes both ways. While website owners need to decide which automated traffic they allow, bot operators need a clear way to identify themselves, explain what their bots do, and keep that information current. BotBase works best when both sides can participate.

When we launched BotBase, we said we would build tools to bring bot operators into this ecosystem. Until now, their experience largely ended at submission. After pressing submit, an operator had no easy way to check the submission's status, understand why it was rejected, or update an existing entry. Today, we start to change that with the launch of BotBase for Operators, tackling what bot operators need first: transparency.

## A new home for bot submissions

Imagine you’re a bot operator looking to submit your bot to [BotBase](https://radar.cloudflare.com/bots/directory). Where on the [dashboard](https://dash.cloudflare.com/) would you look for such a submission form? Previously, the form lived under **Manage Account → Configurations**, which tied the bot clearly to your account, but didn’t acknowledge its connection to the bots ecosystem.

Starting today, the bot submission experience has a home next to the rest of your bot and trust tools: **Protect & Connect → Application Security → BotBase** *(new!)*. All customers can access this today directly from the [Cloudflare dashboard](https://dash.cloudflare.com/?to=/:account/application-security/botbase).

Here, we’ve split BotBase for Operators by use case:

* **Bots directory** — browse, search, and filter the bots Cloudflare already tracks (the same catalogue you can explore on [Cloudflare Radar](https://radar.cloudflare.com/bots/directory)).
* **Submission form** — submit a new bot.
* **Submission history** — track everything you have submitted.

Finding BotBase solves the "where" problem. The "what happens next" problem is the one that we’ve heard is deeply important to bot operators, so we’ll cover that in the rest of this post.

## See where your submission stands

We spoke to many bot operators, and the resounding feedback was this: *submitting a bot feels like a black box*. You fill in the form, press submit, and wait, with no way to tell whether anything happened next.

Now, the **Submission history** tab shows every bot submitted from your account, each with a clear status:

* **Waiting for review** — we have received your submission and it is in our queue.
* **Accepted** — we have reviewed it and your bot is now tracked in the directory.
* **Rejected** — something in the submission needs to change. We tell you why, with steps you can act on, so you can fix it and resubmit.

Open any submission to see its full details. If it was rejected, you will see the reason why. If it was accepted but we adjusted how your bot is classified, you will see what we changed.

Previously, operators would need to email support just to ask whether their bot got reviewed or to check on their submission's progress. That's exactly the gap we’re closing with this new tab.

Today, the submission form is no longer a black box. Every operator can now view the record of every bot they've submitted starting from today’s launch, with a status you can check anytime. We also provide a way to filter “My bots,” from the Bots directory screen, so you can see all bots that have been submitted under the account with which you’re currently logged in.

## Keep your bot's information up to date

A bot's identification details can change over time. You might redesign your website and end up hosting your IP list at a new endpoint. Or you might move from an IP allowlist to signing your traffic with [Web Bot Auth](https://developers.cloudflare.com/bots/reference/bot-verification/web-bot-auth/), and need your entry to match. Before today, the only way to reflect either change was to fill out the whole form again and submit a brand-new entry. Now, you can edit a submission you have already made.

You can also cancel a submission that is still waiting for review.

We encourage every operator to keep their bot's information current. Accurate details are a key component of how a bot earns and keeps [Verified](https://developers.cloudflare.com/bots/concepts/bot/verified-bots/) status, which increasingly determines whether sites across Cloudflare's network can easily allow it based on its behavior. Of course, it is ultimately up to the individual site owner to decide what traffic is allowed and what is not.

## A submission form built on an updated, pragmatic taxonomy

Picture a bot. Maybe it only crawls pages to build a search index. Maybe it also acts on a user's behalf, or pulls in data for something else entirely. How it uses what it reads matters just as much as what it does.

The new intake form asks you to describe your bot the way it actually behaves. It follows the same [behavior and content use model we introduced on July 1](https://blog.cloudflare.com/content-independence-day-ai-options), so instead of squeezing your bot into a single label, you now tell us three things.

First, what your bot does. Maybe it only does one thing, like indexing pages for search. Maybe it's an agent acting on a user's behalf, or it collects data, trains models, or supports SEO tools. You can select every behavior that applies, not just the closest match.

Second, how it uses what it reads. A crawler that skims a page for a search snippet is not the same as one that stores that page to train a model. You tell us the level of content use your bot needs, using the same [Content Signals](https://contentsignals.org) model website owners already use to set their own rules. For example, a site's robots.txt might read Content-Signal: search=yes, ai-train=no, use=reference, telling every crawler it's fine to index the page for search and keep a reference, but not to train a model on it. Your bot's content-use declaration is what gets checked against exactly that kind of preference.

Third, who's actually running it. If you operate your bot yourself, straight from your own infrastructure, like a search engine crawling the web to build its own index, that's direct. If you run a platform other companies build on, carrying their traffic without being the one who decided to send it, that's an intermediary. Picture a general-purpose AI assistant fetching a page because someone typed a question into a different company's app built on that assistant's API: the assistant operator runs the infrastructure, but it was someone else's product that decided to send the request. (You can read more about these classifications [here](https://developers.cloudflare.com/bots/concepts/bot/verified-bots/#classification).)

That's the full picture: what your bot does, how it treats what it reads, and who's behind it, described as it actually is instead of squeezed into one label. The clearer that picture, the more accurately website owners can decide how to treat your bot.

## Faster, more consistent review

Operators also asked for faster reviews. We hear you on this, too.

The number of new bots submitted each year has grown sharply — increasing about 7 times in volume since 2023 — and reviewing every one of them by hand doesn't scale at that pace. Until now, every submission followed the same fully manual path: someone on our team checks it against an internal rubric and makes a judgment call. That kind of review is thorough, but it doesn't scale.

We rebuilt that process to run automatically. Your bot runs through a series of checks — is it a duplicate of one we already track, is your user-agent pattern specific enough to identify your bot without overlapping one that's already registered, and, most importantly, does your claimed verification method actually hold up? We fetch your IP list, confirm your reverse DNS, or validate your [Web Bot Auth](https://developers.cloudflare.com/bots/reference/bot-verification/web-bot-auth/) signature automatically, instead of a person doing it by hand. If everything checks out, your bot can be tracked right away. If something needs a closer look, it's routed to our team with the specific reason already flagged, instead of landing as a blank entry in a queue.

For operators, that means most submissions move faster than before.

## Submit your bot today

To join hundreds of bots in BotBase who declare their behavior and content use, and be part of an ecosystem where website owners and bot operators can coexist:

1. Go to **Protect & Connect → Application Security → BotBase** in the [Cloudflare dashboard](https://dash.cloudflare.com/?to=/:account/application-security/botbase).
2. Open the **Submission form** and declare your bot: who operates it, what it does, how it uses content, and how it proves its identity.
3. Submit. Your submission appears in **Submission history** as *Waiting for review*.

## What's next

This launch is about visibility; there's more coming. Here are our guiding goals:

* **Visibility**, targeted by this launch. This gives operators the ability to see, understand, and edit submissions.
* **Ownership and observability**, being targeted soon. This gives operators the ability to claim bot ownership, manage its live directory entry, and better understand how websites are treating their bot.
* **Conversation**, a longer-term goal. This would open a more sustainable way for bot operators to ask websites to be let in if they can show they provide value rather than harm.

Our vision is to keep expanding BotBase so operators can understand exactly how their bot is treated and get guidance on how to crawl the web more politely, turning a one-way submission into an ongoing relationship.

BotBase started as a directory for website owners. It is becoming a place where bot operators take part in the ecosystem, understand where they stand, and keep their information accurate. If you run a bot, [submit it and tell us what you need next](https://dash.cloudflare.com/?to=/:account/application-security/botbase/directory). We are building the operator side alongside the operators who use it.

entries.title: Datacenters face direct hit from China rare earth curbs, as clock runs out on escalated licensing chokeoff
entries.content: The IEEE is warning that China’s export controls on rare earth minerals could start to impact datacenters, as shipments of some key materials are down 75 percent and Beijing is due to review its policies this November. The techie org's official publication, IEEE Spectrum, focuses on two rare earths in particular, erbium and yttrium, which are used in components for IT equipment. Exports of yttrium are down by about 75 percent this year in comparison with 2025. Yttrium was one of seven medium and heavy rare earth elements that China placed under mandatory licensing in its first wave of restrictions in 2025. Yttrium is used in white LED lights and displays, microwave filters, and solid-state lasers, and also in ceramic capacitors found in pretty much all electronic kit. Erbium is used in the amplifier circuits that boost optical signals in fiber-optic links. The Chinese government enacted restrictions on the overseas sale of rare earth minerals last April, as reported by The Register. This was part of retaliatory measures against the Trump administration’s slapdash trade tariffs. It upped the ante later in the year with tougher measures, including laws that require companies to apply for a license before they ship any goods containing rare earths sourced in China to anywhere in the outside world. This latter rule is a mirror of US laws like those used to block the export of ASML chipmaking equipment to China. That second wave of measures – which was to have included increased export controls of five new elements including erbium – was suspended in November 2025 for 12 months, following trade talks between the US and China. When the year is up this November, Beijing will decide whether to drop the tougher measures or re-apply them, perhaps extending them to all or most of the rare earth minerals it controls. According to the International Energy Agency (IEA), the supply of rare earths remains among the least geographically diversified among all critical minerals. For those minerals used in magnets, China accounted for about 60 percent of global mining output in 2024, and its dominance is even greater in the separation and refining stages, making up about 91 percent of global production. But for yttrium and erbium used in IT kit, China is effectively the sole source, IEEE Spectrum claims. The country mines 90 percent of the world’s yttrium, but it processes all of the world’s mined ore into an industrially usable form such as yttrium oxide, and likewise supplies all erbium oxide. Washington has been taking some steps to try and offset China’s virtual monopoly of key rare earth materials. Recently, the US Department of Defense announced a $750 million investment to secure supplies of rare earth elements for magnets from a production site in central Brazil, while the Department of Energy announced $500 million for seven selected projects to expand critical mineral and material processing, battery manufacturing, and recycling. The US signed agreements with representatives of 54 countries at the 2026 Critical Minerals Ministerial meeting in February this year, as well as talking up commitments to build secure and resilient supply chains for such materials. Also in February, President Trump launched Project Vault, a supply chain security initiative establishing an American Strategic Critical Minerals Reserve stockpile, with funding of up to $10 billion from the federal Export-Import Bank of the United States. But many of these initiatives will take time to have any impact, and China’s impending decision will put these to the test, should it decide to take a tougher stance. Relations between Washingon and Beijing remain strained because of trade and other factors, and a lot could be riding on a summit between President Trump and President Xi Jinping next month. ®

entries.title: Pentagon blacklisted Anthropic over Claude powers it didn't have
entries.content: The Pentagon illegally blacklisted Anthropic as a national security threat based partly on things Claude couldn't actually do, a US federal judge has ruled. US District Judge Rita Lin found that the government illegally retaliated against Anthropic for speaking out, denied the company due process, and unlawfully branded it a supply-chain risk. In a 59-page ruling, she repeatedly picked apart the Pentagon's national security case and found some of its central claims about Claude "entirely unfounded." The dispute erupted in February after Anthropic refused to remove safeguards preventing Claude from being used for certain military applications, including fully autonomous weapons and mass domestic surveillance. At a meeting with Anthropic, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth called Claude's capabilities "exquisite" and said the company's concerns were "understandable," but gave it three days to agree to "all lawful uses" or face being designated a supply-chain risk. Hegseth also floated invoking the Defense Production Act to declare Anthropic essential to national security and compel it to provide Claude. He then announced that Anthropic would be designated a supply-chain risk, while President Trump ordered federal agencies to stop using its technology. One problem: the Pentagon hadn't yet written the assessment explaining why Anthropic supposedly posed that risk. When that assessment arrived, it suggested Anthropic could interfere with Claude during military operations by altering or disabling models, allowing them to "drift," or introducing hidden biases or backdoors. According to the court, Anthropic couldn't actually do those things to Claude models already deployed inside Pentagon systems. Those models are static, and Anthropic cannot remotely access, modify, update, or disable them. The government didn't dispute that evidence, leading Lin to call the alleged danger "entirely unfounded." Years of government records also contained no previous Anthropic supply-chain concerns, said the judge's order. Lin said the chronology suggested the Pentagon assembled its case "after the fact to justify the foreordained conclusion." The government also did not behave as if Anthropic were an intolerable national security threat. Even after the designation was finalized, Under Secretary of Defense Emil Michael was still negotiating contract language with the company. "I think we are very close here," he wrote in an email. The government later continued working with Anthropic around Project Glasswing and its Mythos cybersecurity model. According to the ruling, the NSA and NASA began deploying Mythos, while senior White House officials held what Anthropic described as "productive and constructive" talks with CEO Dario Amodei. Lin instead found substantial evidence that Anthropic had been punished for publicly disagreeing with the administration. Her order cited Trump branding it a "RADICAL LEFT, WOKE COMPANY" staffed by "Leftwing nut jobs," adding that Hegseth spoke of its "Silicon Valley ideology." The Pentagon's own internal memo complained that Anthropic had behaved in an "increasingly hostile manner through the press." Lin said announcing Anthropic's punishment before the formal designation process had begun appeared designed to "make a public example of Anthropic for daring to criticize the Administration." The judge also rejected the idea that being a difficult supplier makes a company a security threat. "An IT vendor does not become a potential adversary of the United States whenever it asks probing questions," she wrote, warning against blacklisting companies simply because officials considered them "too arrogant or difficult to 'trust.'" The consequences went well beyond losing a Pentagon contract. Hegseth's directive sought to prevent Pentagon contractors and suppliers from doing business with Anthropic, even for work unrelated to defense. More than 100 enterprise customers contacted Anthropic with concerns about continuing to work with it, and the company estimated the measures could knock multiple billions of dollars off its 2026 revenue. Lin stressed that the Pentagon remains free to stop buying Anthropic's technology through lawful procurement processes. It couldn't, however, use a contracting dispute to punish a government critic. "The empty invocation of national security is not a blank check to punish and retaliate against government critics," she concluded. ®

entries.title: Opinion | How Shenzhen can win the ‘AI for science’ race | South China Morning Post
entries.content: The United States made that shift explicit. The Department of Energy’s Genesis Mission aims to bring together 17 national laboratories into an integrated discovery platform to double the productivity and impact of US research and innovation within a decade. This year, the programme announced a partnership with Japan, reinforcing the idea that AI for science is becoming infrastructure and a network, not simply another model. [...] The next big competition in artificial intelligence is over science. The question is shifting from who has the largest model to who can use AI to shorten the discovery cycle: forming a hypothesis, running simulations, designing an experiment, operating equipment, collecting results and learning from them. [...] China is moving in the same direction but increasingly through cities. Beijing’s 2025 plan calls for common scientific-intelligence infrastructure, at least 10 high-quality scientific databases, more than 10 million users and at least eight benchmark applications by 2027. entries.title: Sam Altman needs to put up or shut up about AI hacking
entries.content:
In what is likely the most tone-deaf response by companies that have created a massive problem, Sam Altman and other AI companies are crying out for a public effort to solve AI hacking that they all enabled.  
  

![Two people in a black-and-white portrait, one wearing glasses and resting their head on the other's shoulder, both with neutral expressions.](https://photos5.appleinsider.com/gallery/64318-134009-iveandalt-xl.jpg)  
Jony Ive & Sam Altman | Image Credit: OpenAI

  
What an absolute crock of self-serving nonsense from OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, again.  
  
What Altman is likely referring to in a post on X, and ignoring the fire in his own house, is that a Chinese company is about to release a new "frontier coding with emergent cyber capabilities model."

entries.title: Best Retina-class displays to pair with Mac mini or Mac studio
entries.content:
There are thousands of external displays, but only a small fraction fit the criteria of being a Retina display. From smaller 4K options to Apple's high-end [Studio Display](https://appleinsider.com/inside/studio-display "Studio Display") XDR, you have plenty of displays to choose from at nearly every price point.  
  

![Desktop computer with large monitor displaying a bald man giving an online presentation in a guitar shop, with a small white computer tower below, on a colorful blurred background](https://media.appleinsider.com/gallery/68745-144811-headerimage-xl.jpg)  
Best monitors for Mac mini and Mac Studio

  
If you're planning to pick up a new Mac mini or [Mac Studio](https://appleinsider.com/inside/mac-studio "Mac Studio"), it might be time to upgrade your monitor setup. Fortunately, the market is flush with options.  
  
Not all of them are "Retina" quality. Given how Apple handles hiDPI monitors without additional software, that leads to problems for some users with text crispness. It's certainly not a case for everyone, but if it is for you, and you don't want to install something like [BetterDisplay](https://betterdisplay.pro), there are some clear choices.

entries.title: Apple's latest price hike is to Apple TV streaming and Apple One
entries.content:
Apple's latest round of price increases isn't for hardware, but for Apple TV video streaming and, correspondingly, some [Apple One](https://appleinsider.com/inside/apple-one "Apple One") tiers.  
  

![Apple TV logo with a gradient effect on a black background.](https://photos5.appleinsider.com/gallery/65625-137365-This-is-just-the-beginning0-4-screenshot-xl.jpg)  
The new Apple TV logo

  
Announced on Friday, Apple TV's monthly cost is increasing by $2 to $14.99 per month. This raises the annual cost to $119, up from $99.  
  
This affects some Apple One subscriptions as well. While the family plan monthly cost isn't going up, the individual plan is.

## Milwaukee cutoff tool

A cutoff tool can be used for DIY projects like trimming off a rusted-out bolt or trimming PVC drain parts to fit for a DIY plumbing project. Make sure to wear a face shield when you’re operating a cutoff tool to avoid injury in the event that the cutting disc shatters or the material you’re cutting splinters. The [Milwaukee 12-volt cutoff tool](https://zdcs.link/z6xxqR?pageview_type=RSS&template=content&module=content_body&element=offer&item=text-link&element_label=Milwaukee%2012-volt%20cutoff%20tool&object_type=content&short_url=z6xxqR&u=https%3A%2F%2Flifehacker.com%2Ffeed%2Frss "open in a new window") is on sale for $189, 57% off its usual price. This is a good tool for small projects where you need to cut metal, PVC, or tile. Because of its smaller size, it can be a little easier to use this tool in tight spaces like under a sink. ## Milwaukee cordless electric ratchet

An electric ratchet can give you torque without needing space to turn your wrench. It can be handy working on cars or doing your own maintenance on appliances, like taking the cover off of a vent in an awkward spot. The [Milwaukee 12-volt cordless electric ⅜-inch ratchet](https://zdcs.link/QGjjxV?pageview_type=RSS&template=content&module=content_body&element=offer&item=text-link&element_label=Milwaukee%2012-volt%20cordless%20electric%20%E2%85%9C-inch%20ratchet&object_type=content&short_url=QGjjxV&u=https%3A%2F%2Flifehacker.com%2Ffeed%2Frss "open in a new window") is now $189, 59% off its regular price. The trigger on this tool will change the amount of force you’re applying depending on how hard you squeeze it; it can get up to about 35 foot-pounds of torque. The choice really comes down to whether you care more about gaming features or getting the biggest screen for your money. The M80H is the more capable option on paper, with HDMI 2.1 bandwidth and a 144Hz refresh rate, so it makes more sense if you plan to connect a newer console or gaming PC. Even then, I would not buy it just for the 144Hz label, because its slower pixel response can still make fast motion look blurry.

The 75-inch [M70H](https://zdcs.link/QVJJ4L?pageview_type=RSS&template=content&module=content_body&element=offer&item=text-link&element_label=M70H&object_type=content&short_url=QVJJ4L&u=https%3A%2F%2Flifehacker.com%2Ffeed%2Frss "open in a new window") is easier to understand as a size-first buy. At $549.99, it gives you a lot of screen for a family room where most of the time will be spent streaming shows, watching sports, or putting on movies rather than chasing high frame rates. Neither TV is especially strong in a dark room, though, since both lack true local dimming and their lower contrast can make black scenes look more gray than black. They also struggle more with glare in brighter rooms, so placement matters if your living room gets a lot of daylight. The [M80H](https://zdcs.link/zEKKo4?pageview_type=RSS&template=content&module=content_body&element=offer&item=text-link&element_label=M80H&object_type=content&short_url=zEKKo4&u=https%3A%2F%2Flifehacker.com%2Ffeed%2Frss "open in a new window") at least has good out-of-box color accuracy for standard content, while Samsung’s smart TV platform means both sets can handle the usual streaming apps without needing another device.

That is also why I would treat these as value buys rather than obvious upgrades. The M70H makes sense if your priority is simply getting a 75-inch TV for around $550, while the M80H is the better fit if you specifically want HDMI 2.1 and a higher refresh rate. Anyone more focused on HDR, black levels, or gaming performance should also look at [alternatives](https://lifehacker.com/tech/best-65-inch-tvs) like the [TCL QM6K](https://zdcs.link/9gJJ1y?pageview_type=RSS&template=content&module=content_body&element=offer&item=text-link&element_label=TCL%20QM6K&object_type=content&short_url=9gJJ1y&u=https%3A%2F%2Flifehacker.com%2Ffeed%2Frss "open in a new window") or [Hisense U65QF](https://zdcs.link/akjjX6?pageview_type=RSS&template=content&module=content_body&element=offer&item=text-link&element_label=Hisense%20U65QF&object_type=content&short_url=akjjX6&u=https%3A%2F%2Flifehacker.com%2Ffeed%2Frss "open in a new window"), since both add local dimming and stronger overall picture performance, making either a better fit for someone prioritizing picture quality over the Samsung name.

Garmin's lineup of [fitness trackers](https://mashable.com/roundup/best-fitness-trackers-1) just got bigger and more impressive. The Garmin Fenix 9 and Garmin Fenix 9 Pro are the brand's latest offerings, designed to help us "play harder." Launched via an in-depth YouTube video, the new lineup features a thinner design, better durability, a built-in flashlight, and a few new features that'll appeal to [fitness](https://mashable.com/category/fitness) fanatics.

The Garmin Fenix 9 and both the standard and solar versions of the Fenix 9 Pro are available to buy from Aug. 28. Here's a breakdown of features and details to consider before you buy.

## Key features of the Garmin Fenix 9

With each new model, we're always looking for the key differences compared to the previous model. In this case, Garmin made the Fenix 9 slimmer and more durable, without adding much weight at all. Garmin Epic is new to the upgraded Fenix 9 family. The feature allows you to group activities into a single story rather than as individual activities. Consider a multi-day hike or a 100-mile bike ride split into two days. Garmin can now group these activities to give you a broader overview of the adventure, including sleep data, mileage, and the event's impact on endurance and stamina.

![a topographic map displayed on the garmin fenix 9](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/02iicSmQLLVxPBAGcBjOLRh/images-3.fill.size_2000x1292.v1787923241.jpg)

The Fenix 9 lineup features better mapping and navigational tools.
Credit: Garmin

Garmin also noted that many of us have developed a special liking for [rowing](https://mashable.com/article/sept-16-hydrow-arc-rower), especially those training for Hyrox. To meet this demand, Garmin incorporated improved performance data for rowing. For those heading out on the trail, Garmin added more intuitive routable maps.

The standard Garmin Fenix 9 can get up to 16 days of battery life in smartwatch mode and will launch with a list price of $999.99 on Aug. 28.

## Key features of the Garmin Fenix 9 Pro and Fenix 9 Pro Solar

To clear things up right away, both the Fenix 9 Pro and Fenix 9 Pro Solar are identical in specs except for the solar recharging. One of the coolest things about this is that Garmin isn't charging us more for the solar-powered Pro option. Both the Fenix 9 Pro and Fenix 9 Pro Solar will cost $1,099.99 in the 47mm sizes and $1,199.99 in the larger 51mm size.

Compared to the standard Garmin Fenix 9, the Pro and Pro Solar have a brighter screen and an LED flashlight onboard that can illuminate in dimmable white, green, or red. The Fenix 9 can only display in dimmable white. The Pro and Pro Solar are also one gram lighter than the Fenix 9, and slightly thinner.

![a row of new garmin fenix 9 watches](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/02iicSmQLLVxPBAGcBjOLRh/images-4.fill.size_2000x861.v1787923241.jpg)

The latest models in Garmin's product offerings: The Fenix 9 and Fenix 9 Pro
Credit: Garmin

The Pro also has a larger battery, and Garmin says it can last up to 18 days in [smartwatch](https://mashable.com/article/best-smartwatches-2025-tested) mode. Of course, the Fenix 9 Pro Solar has a solar-charging lens that can earn you up to 34 days of battery life in smartwatch mode.

In addition to these physical features, the Pro and Pro Solar also come with the tech and fitness-tracking upgrades mentioned above for the Garmin Fenix 9, such as more advanced rowing performance data, the ability to group activities with Garmin Epic, an endurance score, and better stamina tracking.

## How to buy the Garmin Fenix 9 and Garmin Fenix 9 Pro

Garmin officially announced this new lineup on Aug. 25, but shoppers had to wait a few days before they could place orders.

The Garmin website now lists these models as [available to buy](https://zdcs.link/a0M775?pageview_type=RSS&template=article&module=content_body&element=offer&item=text-link&element_label=available%20to%20buy&object_type=article&object_uuid=02iicSmQLLVxPBAGcBjOLRh&short_url=a0M775&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmashable.com%2Ffeeds%2Frss%2Fall "(opens in a new window)"). We'll keep an eye on availability at Amazon, Best Buy, and other retailers. We have a feeling we'll see more retailers add these new Garmin models now that they're available for purchase.

entries.title: Is AdultFriendFinder legit? Only if you can follow these 4 rules.
entries.content:
![Couple woith feet coming out of bed](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/00O1g4eeEtCGFVlnQy1im9l/hero-image.jpg)

As one of the true OGs of online dating, [AdultFriendFinder](https://zdcs.link/a0Xvw?pageview_type=RSS&template=article&module=content_body&element=offer&item=text-link&element_label=AdultFriendFinder&object_type=article&object_uuid=00O1g4eeEtCGFVlnQy1im9l&short_url=a0Xvw&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmashable.com%2Ffeeds%2Frss%2Fall "(opens in a new window)") has a sizeable community of [singles](https://mashable.com/article/single-for-decade-lessons) and non-monogamous users [looking for steamy fun](https://mashable.com/roundup/best-hookup-apps). But that doesn’t mean using the site is necessarily straightforward. In fact, AFF, as its users call it, has been online for so long that its web interface can feel dated and counterintuitive, with key features requiring you to navigate a whole manner of menus and sub-menus.

Making the most of AFF means a certain amount of trial and error, or at least some guidance from someone with an intimate knowledge of the spicy hookup platform.

That's why we've outlined four essential tips below to get you up and running on AFF and help connect with more people for more kink-filled fun. That said, it also helps to keep an open mind about it all. If you enter AFF with a narrow idea of exactly what you want, you'll likely be disappointed. But if you start your search with an open-minded curiosity and just go along for the ride (pun very much intended), you can discover new things about yourself — and maybe even your pleasure points — in the process.

[![AdultFriendFinder logo](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/00O1g4eeEtCGFVlnQy1im9l/images-1.fill.size_256x134.v1771345441.png)

Opens in a new window](https://zdcs.link/a0Xvw?pageview_type=RSS&template=article&module=shop-card&element=offer&item=image&element_label=image&object_type=article&object_uuid=00O1g4eeEtCGFVlnQy1im9l&short_url=a0Xvw&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmashable.com%2Ffeeds%2Frss%2Fall "(opens in a new window)")

Credit: AdultFriendFinder

[AdultFriendFinder](https://zdcs.link/a0Xvw?pageview_type=RSS&template=article&module=shop-card&element=offer&item=title&element_label=AdultFriendFinder&object_type=article&object_uuid=00O1g4eeEtCGFVlnQy1im9l&short_url=a0Xvw&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmashable.com%2Ffeeds%2Frss%2Fall "(opens in a new window)")

[Learn More](https://zdcs.link/a0Xvw?pageview_type=RSS&template=article&module=shop-card&element=offer&item=buy-button&element_label=Get%20Deal&object_type=article&object_uuid=00O1g4eeEtCGFVlnQy1im9l&short_url=a0Xvw&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmashable.com%2Ffeeds%2Frss%2Fall "(opens in a new window)")

Here are four essential steps for getting the most out of your [AdultFriendFinder](https://zdcs.link/a0Xvw?pageview_type=RSS&template=article&module=content_body&element=offer&item=text-link&element_label=AdultFriendFinder&object_type=article&object_uuid=00O1g4eeEtCGFVlnQy1im9l&short_url=a0Xvw&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmashable.com%2Ffeeds%2Frss%2Fall "(opens in a new window)") experience:

### Fill out your full AFF profile

Sure, this is an obvious step with any and every [online dating service](https://mashable.com/roundup/best-dating-apps-2026), but it’s even more important on AFF because the site doesn’t entirely rely on a carousel-style presentation of [dating profiles](https://mashable.com/article/what-is-raya-dating-app) like other apps. Everything from your age to your gender to your sexuality to your list of personal kinks can help make you more discoverable to other AFF members, so the less you fill out, the harder it is for the site to make your profile discoverable.

This is true even if your personal kink list is short or leans towards the conventional, or if it’s long and girthy and leans towards the exotic; trust us when we say there are people out there who are looking for the very same quirks and kinks and sexuality specifics, so it's worth taking your time to be specific and details. It will pay off in the long run.

SEE ALSO:
[Is Hinge really 'designed to be deleted'? I tested it to find out.](https://mashable.com/review/hinge-dating-app-review)

Also, don’t sleep on videos. Unlike many [dating sites](https://mashable.com/roundup/best-dating-apps-for-serious-relationships) that allow only profile pictures, AFF permits its members to upload short videos to their profiles. This is a fantastic way of showing others that you’re a real person — as opposed to a bot, which you'll find plenty of on AFF — and also helps you show off some personality. Just be wary of putting [nude content](https://mashable.com/article/common-hookup-site-profile-mistakes) upfront in your profile. You can do this if you wish, of course — AFF is all about the NSFW content — but putting that kind of content out there does raise privacy issues.

### Verify your AFF account as soon as possible

[AdultFriendFinder](https://zdcs.link/a0Xvw?pageview_type=RSS&template=article&module=content_body&element=offer&item=text-link&element_label=AdultFriendFinder&object_type=article&object_uuid=00O1g4eeEtCGFVlnQy1im9l&short_url=a0Xvw&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmashable.com%2Ffeeds%2Frss%2Fall "(opens in a new window)") throws up very few barriers when you're creating your account. That makes it very easy for anyone to join, but it also means there is a huge amount of spam and bots clogging up the platform. To combat this, they’ve also created a profile verification system using the Confirm ID service.

It requires you to [share government ID](https://mashable.com/article/all-the-states-and-countries-with-age-verification-laws) for cast-iron verification, but the benefits to your profile will give you major peace of mind. It means photo authentication, age confirmation, and location verification, all of which help others trust that your profile is authentic. When the process is complete, you'll see a blue checkmark beneath your profile photo, just to the right of your username, which helps people identify your profile at a glance and boosts your visibility in search results, as search results prioritize verified users.

### Be selective with your search criteria

If you use the site’s search function, you’ll find that you can be extremely specific and selective. And if you know exactly who and what you want, by all means, narrow your search, but if you’re on AFF to be surprised, it’s also worth being less selective from time to time.

For example, if you know you want an in-person date for next week, it obviously makes sense to narrow your location search to people who live near you. But what if you don’t know exactly what you want, or if you’re open to a sultry chat with a stranger half a world away? In that case, distance is irrelevant, and you should consider turning that filter off.

SEE ALSO:
[All your Tinder questions, answered](https://mashable.com/article/what-is-tinder-questions-answered)

On the other hand, there are quite a few filters that are turned off by default that we actually recommend you turn on. For example, the default profile filter shows you all people who have bothered to upload photos, but while that’s a good start, it’s not enough to help you wade through the huge number of users. We strongly recommend narrowing it down to Verified/Confirmed users, since those people all proved their identity the same way you did (see above). That way, you can trust that your search results and potential connections are 100 percent legit. It's another means of filtering out the spam.

Another useful filter is the Last Visit, which by default is set to "All." We recommend specifying accounts that have been active within the last month. That's because lots of people sign up to AFF then never bother checking back in. Other users go inactive for weeks or even months at a time. If you stick with the default "All" setting, you risk [messaging](https://mashable.com/roundup/best-sexting-apps-2026) accounts that you might never get a reply from.

### Explore the live-chat communities

AdultFriendFinder isn’t a traditional dating website, so don't use it like one. The search-and-swipe dating app method is tried and true, but it’s also a bit played out, and one of AFF’s biggest strengths is its larger community offerings. There's more to it than swiping — or should we say swinging? — left or right.

There are lots of forums to explore, all based around common interests (though you should know that some of these interests — or kinks — are not so common), or you can venture into a user’s livestream and interact with them and others there. AFF even has a dedicated Stories section, where users can share their memories or try their hand at writing erotica. That's all well and good for anyone with a knack for the written word, but if you're more visual, you can set up a webcam stream and invite others to tune in.

For all of the above, AFF tracks not only which stories/streams/group chats are new but also which are trending, making it very easy to jump into a popular discussion or keep up with the latest site news.

### Upgrade your AFF membership tier

As with other dating sites and apps, you only get the most out of AFF when you sign up for a [paid membership](https://zdcs.link/a0Xvw?pageview_type=RSS&template=article&module=content_body&element=offer&item=text-link&element_label=paid%20membership&object_type=article&object_uuid=00O1g4eeEtCGFVlnQy1im9l&short_url=a0Xvw&u=https%3A%2F%2Fmashable.com%2Ffeeds%2Frss%2Fall "(opens in a new window)"). It is entirely possible to use AFF and interact without handing over your credit card information, but the site’s best features and functions are paywalled. And it has to be said that the advantages — visibility, communication options, and site functionality are all just too good to ignore.

Gold and VIP members receive special icons on their profiles, and these profiles are given priority in every search, regardless of the criteria. Because there are thousands of potential profile options for almost every search criterion that isn’t location-based, it’s very difficult to stand out from the crowd on AFF as a free user.

Additionally, if you fork out for the upgraded VIP membership, you’ll unlock an entire section dedicated exclusively to VIPs. It's the dating site equivalent of entering the velvet-roped area of a night club; you'll find the most glamorous people hiding there. VIP members even get additional points to spend on digital gifts or lavish on live streamers who catch your eye. This is another great way of standing out from the crowd.

The learning curve on AdultFriendFinder is steeper than most other dating sites, and much steeper than most dating apps, but if you follow the above tips and you're willing to experiment, you’ll encounter more than a few fun and sexy surprises along the way.

entries.content: I am juggling two Frontiers now, one the last release of the OPML editor from 2014, and the other the in-development version codenamed Atlantis that runs in Electron and thus is built on JavaScript and Chrome. Took me a while to get over the confusion, because Frontier is actually a product that contains other products and the common layers they need to be on the web. And I just realized I may not need Electric Drummer, because Atlantis uses the same outliner as Drummer. I was stockpiling all these Node packages and user interface stuff that now is relevant in the uber-framework, the one I aimed to spend the rest of my life working in. Well maybe it'll turn out that there was just a 12 year vacation? It's all very confusing and all my carts are turning over, all the assumptions change. My goal is to get this wonderful product running on my new Mac laptop I currently mainly use for email. I bought it to give reality to the idea of getting on modern hardware and not have to leave behind my bespoke platform. That's what you get if you get through 50 productive years of software development. Your own freaking world.

entries.title: U.S. CISA adds ownCloud, Linux Kernel, and JFrog Artifactory flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog
entries.content:
## U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) adds ownCloud, Linux Kernel, and JFrog Artifactory flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.

The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) [added](https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/alerts/2026/08/27/cisa-adds-three-known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog) the following vulnerabilities to its [Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog](https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog):

* [CVE-2023-49105](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2023-49105) ownCloud Improper Authentication Vulnerability
* [CVE-2026-53362](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-53362) Linux Kernel Unspecified Vulnerability
* [CVE-2026-66384](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-66384) JFrog Artifactory Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory Vulnerability

CVE-2023-49105 (CVSS score of 9.8) is an improper-authentication flaw in ownCloud Server’s WebDAV functionality. An unauthenticated attacker who knows a victim’s username can read, alter, or delete that user’s files when no signing key is configured, because the application can accept pre-signed URLs without properly validating that condition. The issue affects ownCloud core versions 10.6.0 through 10.13.0, before version 10.13.1.

Organisations running affected ownCloud instances should treat remediation as urgent, review exposed WebDAV services, and investigate unusual file access, deletion, modification, or downloads.

CVE-2026-53362 (CVSS score of 7.8) is an out-of-bounds memory-write vulnerability in the Linux kernel’s IPv6 networking subsystem. A local attacker who can create UDP sockets could exploit an incorrect parameter-length calculation during fragmented IPv6 packet handling to overwrite kernel memory, potentially causing a system crash, corrupting data, or escalating privileges.access.

Shortly after the [Hugging Face](https://securityaffairs.com/tag/hugging-face) incident became public, OpenAI said its models had identified and exploited a zero-day vulnerability in JFrog’s Artifactory package registry manager.

The report also describes a separate incident on July 19. In that case, some AI agents exploited the Linux kernel vulnerability, CVE-2026-53362, to gain higher privileges inside an OpenAI environment.

The agents detected that the Linux kernel on their machine was vulnerable, found a public exploit, modified it to work in their environment, and used it to gain root access to the underlying worker node. This allowed them to escape the Artifactory container and move laterally to other parts of the connected environment.

CVE-2026-66384 (CVSS score of 5.3) is a path-traversal vulnerability in JFrog Artifactory’s Docker cache handling. Under specific remote-repository conditions, an authenticated user can manipulate a file path and write data outside the intended cache directory, potentially affecting other locations on the Artifactory host.

According to [Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 22-01: Reducing the Significant Risk of Known Exploited Vulnerabilities](https://cyber.dhs.gov/bod/22-01/), FCEB agencies have to address the identified vulnerabilities by the due date to protect their networks against attacks exploiting the flaws in the catalog.

Experts also recommend that private organizations review the [Catalog](https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog) and address the vulnerabilities in their infrastructure.

CISA orders federal agencies to fix the flaw [CVE-2026-66384](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-66384) by September 10, while the remaining must be addressed by August, 30, 2026.

[**Pierluigi Paganini**](http://www.linkedin.com/pub/pierluigi-paganini/b/742/559)
